# Awesome Neural ISP [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re)

**Neural (learned) camera ISPs with released code and pretrained weights, plus a primer on the classical pipeline they build on.**

A curated list of research on neural (learned) camera image signal processors (ISPs). It covers learned replacements for each stage of the classical pipeline (denoising, demosaicing, white balance, color and tone), end-to-end RAW-to-sRGB networks, controllable neural ISPs, inverse ISPs, ISPs for machine vision, and ISP tuning. For every paper the list records whether code and pretrained weights are public, and links the weights exactly as the official repository does.

It currently holds **417 unique publications**, of which **206 have public code** and **133 release pretrained weights**, plus 29 datasets. The [interactive page](https://ruilin.li/Awesome-Neural-ISP/) has the same data with filters for task, model family, training, signal, control interface and release status. Each publication has one primary task; controllable and mobile/efficient ISPs are overlapping collections. Two challenge implementations are nested under their reports and are not counted as separate publications.

Code and weight totals include explicitly labeled third-party implementations; the weights index includes 1 such publication(s).

**Literature update: 2026-10-28.** The full code/weight audit date remains 2026-10-11; see [sources and update notes](guide/literature-update-2026-10-28.md) for newly checked entries.

**Summary revision: 2026-11-05; classification audit: 2026-11-05.** See the [classification rules and full audit](guide/classification-2026-11-05.md) and [summary revision notes](guide/summary-revision-2026-11-05.md).

**Reading the tables.** In each section, papers with downloadable weights come first. The *Weights* column copies the links from each repository README; "in repo" means the checkpoint files are committed to the repository. In the *Code* column, "unofficial" marks a third-party implementation, "coming soon" a placeholder repository, and "—" means no public code was found.

## ISP 101

A camera sensor records a noisy, linear mosaic with one color per pixel. The ISP turns it into a display-ready image.
The classical stages below are where learned methods plug in; the [full primer](guide/isp-101.md) explains each stage
and comes with a [50-line NumPy pipeline](guide/minimal_isp.py) you can run on your own RAW files.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S[Sensor RAW] --> B[Black level] --> N[Denoise] --> W[White balance] --> D[Demosaic] --> C[Color matrix] --> T[Tone and gamma] --> O[sRGB]
```

| Classical stage | What it does | Learned methods in this list |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Black level, defect pixels, lens shading | remove sensor offsets and optical falloff | usually kept classical |
| Denoising | remove Poisson-Gaussian sensor noise | [Denoising & noise](#raw-denoising--noise-modeling) · [Low-light & exposure](#low-light-rendering--exposure-correction) · [Burst / HDR](#burst--hdr-imaging) · [RAW video](#raw-video) |
| Demosaicing | interpolate the two missing colors per pixel | [Demosaic / remosaic](#demosaicing--remosaicing) |
| White balance | estimate and cancel the illuminant color | [Color / tone / editing](#color-correction-tone--retouching) |
| Color correction, tone, gamma | map camera RGB to sRGB and compress dynamic range | [Color / tone / editing](#color-correction-tone--retouching) |
| The whole pipeline | RAW in, sRGB out | [End-to-end ISP](#end-to-end-raw-to-srgb) · [Mobile / efficient](#mobile--efficient-isp) |
| Explicit rendering controls | user editing, camera conditioning and modular stages | [Controllable ISP](#controllable-neural-isp) |
| The pipeline in reverse | sRGB back to RAW | [Inverse ISP / RAW synthesis](#inverse-isp--raw-synthesis) |
| Output for machines, not people | detection or segmentation on RAW | [Machine vision](#isp-for-machine-vision) |
| Parameters of a hardware ISP | automatic tuning | [ISP optimization](#isp-parameter--pipeline-optimization) |

## Research Threads

- **CNNs, attention and generative ISPs.** The library includes pyramidal CNN pipelines, Transformer and state-space restoration, and diffusion, flow-matching or autoregressive rendering/reconstruction. These families coexist and address different quality, training and deployment constraints. <sub>Examples: PyNET · LiteISPNet · LDM-ISP · RAW-Flow · Retinex-RAWMamba · VAR-ISP</sub>
- **Learning with imperfect or missing pairs.** Cross-camera RAW and RGB captures can differ in geometry and color. Alignment-aware losses, synthetic training data and sensor-domain translation address different parts of this problem. MAI 2025 and NTIRE 2026 include explicit unpaired smartphone-ISP settings. <sub>Examples: LiteISPNet · Unprocessing · Day-to-Night · Rawformer · NTIRE 2026 Unpaired ISP</sub>
- **Capture-aware conditioning.** EXIF settings, device embeddings, calibrated color matrices and capture time provide different conditioning signals. Their presence does not automatically imply exposed user editing controls. <sub>Examples: ParamISP · MetaISP · Uni-ISP · CRISPnet · CCMNet · Time-Aware AWB</sub>
- **Deployment depends on hardware.** Mobile ISP challenges evaluate target-device execution, while compact and binarized designs also appear in denoising, demosaicing and video. Parameter counts, quantization and measured latency answer different efficiency questions. <sub>Examples: MicroISP · PyNET-V2 Mobile · PMRID · BRVE · BinRVR · BMTNet</sub>
- **Imaging for perception and action.** Task-driven rendering, direct RAW inference, learned pipeline selection and input adapters optimize information for downstream models. Benchmarks span detection, segmentation, matching and robotic manipulation. <sub>Examples: Dirty Pixels · AdaptiveISP · RAW-Adapter · TA-ISP · POS-ISP · RawVLA</sub>
- **Different meanings of controllability.** User parameters, reference-style adjustment, replaceable learned stages and camera conditioning are labeled separately in the controllable collection. Color-only editing, inverse reconstruction and automatic tuning remain connected through independent tags. <sub>Examples: CtrlISP · Modular Neural ISP · DRIFT · Deep-FlexISP · Neural Photo-Finishing · ParamISP</sub>

## Cross-task Collections

Collections overlap primary tasks; their counts are not added to the publication total.

### Controllable Neural ISP

Learned rendering with explicit user parameters, style/reference controls, replaceable learned stages or camera-conditioned outputs. Control badges distinguish interactive editing from camera conditioning. Color-only modules and conventional parameter-tuning baselines remain in their own categories.

### End-to-End RAW-to-sRGB

Learned full-pipeline RAW-to-display rendering. Specialized low-light, multi-frame, video and task-driven objectives have their own primary categories. Mobile deployment and controllability are cross-cutting collections.

|:--|:--|:--|
| **[RGB-Event ISP: The Dataset and Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19129)**<br><sub>To establish event-guided ISP evaluation, releases 3,373 pixel-aligned RAW/event captures across 24 scenes, a ColorChecker-referenced conventional pipeline, learned-ISP baselines and a simple event-guided model for studying event contributions. <i>Note: Dataset on HF yunfanlu/RGB-Event-ISP-Dataset and Baidu; non-commercial research use only</i></sub> | ICLR 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/yunfanLu/RGB-Event-ISP) |
| **[Enhancing RAW-to-sRGB with Decoupled Style Structure in Fourier Domain](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02161)**<br><sub>To avoid coupling cross-camera color and spatial reconstruction, separates Fourier phase enhancement, amplitude refinement and color adaptation into three subnetworks; this lets structure and appearance be optimized independently before fusion. <i>Note: README explicitly states checkpoints will not be released; you need to train it yourself</i></sub> | AAAI 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/alexhe101/FourierISP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[SYENet: A Simple Yet Effective Network for Multiple Low-Level Vision Tasks with Real-time Performance on Mobile Device](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2023/html/Gou_SYENet_A_Simple_Yet_Effective_Network_for_Multiple_Low-Level_Vision_ICCV_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To run several low-level vision tasks on mobile hardware, uses two asymmetric branches joined by a quadratic connection unit and a regression focal loss; a roughly 6K-parameter architecture handles ISP, enhancement and super-resolution. <i>Note: README describes the arguments for loading pretrained models, but no weight download link was found; includes an ONNX export script</i></sub> | ICCV 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/sanechips-multimedia/syenet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[PyNet-V2 Mobile: Efficient On-Device Photo Processing With Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.06263)**<br><sub>To enable on-device full-resolution neural ISP, redesigns the CNN for mobile operator and accelerator constraints; evaluates 12MP RAW rendering on Fujifilm UltraISP, including smartphone CPU/GPU and NPU/APU latency measurements. <i>Note: The pretrained model (Google Drive) linked in the README returns 404 (checked 2026-10-11).</i></sub> | ICPR 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/gmalivenko/PyNET-v2)<br><sub>TensorFlow / Keras</sub> |
| **[CameraNet: A Two-Stage Framework for Effective Camera ISP Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.01481)**<br><sub>To separate conflicting restoration and aesthetic objectives, uses two CNN modules with distinct supervision and progressive training: one restores sensor measurements, while the other learns color and appearance enhancement. <i>Note: Official TF1.15 code; README only provides HDR+/SID processed data, no weight link found</i></sub> | IEEE TIP 2019 | [GitHub](https://github.com/zhetongliang/CameraNet_official)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> |
| **[HighEr-Resolution Network for Image Demosaicing and Enhancing](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.08098)**<br><sub>To exploit large patches without excessive GPU memory, combines parallel high- and low-resolution feature paths for local detail and global context; progressive training stabilizes joint demosaicing and enhancement. <i>Note: Both OneDrive links for the challenge weights (114.pth / 115.pth) in the README return 404 (checked 2026-10-11).</i></sub> | ICCVW (AIM) 2019 | [GitHub](https://github.com/MKFMIKU/RAW2RGBNet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Freeze the Structure, Free the Color: Fourier-Domain Training for Unpaired Smartphone ISP](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2026W/NTIRE/html/Kim_Freeze_the_Structure_Free_the_Color_Fourier-Domain_Training_for_Unpaired_CVPRW_2026_paper.html)**<br><sub>To prevent unpaired color learning from damaging geometry, stabilizes and freezes FourierISP's structural branch, then trains color with a blurred-image ViT discriminator, inverse-cycle consistency and VGG perceptual losses under a staged curriculum.</sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2026 | — |
| **[RPBA-Net: An Interpretable Residual Pyramid Bilateral Affine Network for RAW-Domain ISP Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03626)**<br><sub>To make RAW enhancement interpretable and compact, predicts identity-guided residual affine corrections and pyramid bilateral grids; guide-driven adaptive slicing and cross-scale fusion jointly reconstruct color, global tone and local texture.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[Visual Autoregressive Priors for RAW-to-sRGB Image Signal Processing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18302)**<br><sub>To exploit generative priors despite imperfect alignment and missing metadata, adapts a frozen visual-autoregressive next-scale predictor to RAW conditioning; wavelet-separated color losses supervise low-frequency tone and chromatic edges with limited trainable parameters.</sub> | ECCVW (LoViF) 2026 | — |
| **[EvRAW: Event-guided Structural and Color Modeling for RAW-to-sRGB Image Reconstruction](https://doi.org/10.1145/3746027.3754983)**<br><sub>To reduce motion blur and color distortion in dynamic RAW-to-sRGB imaging, extracts event-motion cues with a structural-enhancement module and uses regional gamma/channel-wise color decoding; contributes pixel-aligned RAW/event data.</sub> | ACM MM 2025 | — |
| **[Experts-Guided Unbalanced Optimal Transport for ISP Learning from Unpaired and/or Paired Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.05635)**<br><sub>To reduce dependence on paired RAW–sRGB captures, trains existing ISP architectures with unbalanced optimal transport and a committee of color, structure and frequency discriminators; supports paired or unpaired learning while discounting target-domain outliers. <i>Note: Repo currently contains only a README</i></sub> | arXiv 2025 | [GitHub (coming soon)](https://github.com/gosha20777/EGUOT-ISP) |
| **[SemiISP/SemiIE: Semi-Supervised Image Signal Processor and Image Enhancement Leveraging One-to-Many Mapping sRGB-to-RAW](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02345)**<br><sub>To train personalized ISPs with few paired captures, learns a one-to-many sRGB-to-RAW reconstruction model and uses its synthetic pairs alongside real pairs in semi-supervised training, extending the approach to image enhancement.</sub> | arXiv 2025 | — |
| **[Uni-ISP: Toward Unifying the Learning of ISPs from Multiple Mobile Cameras](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.01003)**<br><sub>To avoid a separate neural ISP for every camera, conditions jointly learned forward/inverse mappings on device embeddings; releases synchronized FiveCam RAW–sRGB pairs and evaluates adaptation to new devices and cross-camera rendering.</sub> | IEEE TIP 2025 | — |
| **[RMFA-Net: A Neural ISP for Real RAW to RGB Image Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11469)**<br><sub>To respect RAW sensor structure and uneven exposure, combines implicit black-level correction, a three-channel split preserving CFA detail and Retinex-based explicit tone mapping; also provides a smaller deployment variant.</sub> | arXiv 2024 | — |
| **[Simple Image Signal Processing using Global Context Guidance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.11569)**<br><sub>To recover global illumination cues lost during patch training, adds a full-RAW global-context module to a compact neural ISP; the module can also augment other backbones to improve full-image color and tone consistency.</sub> | ICIP 2024 | — |
| **[CRISPnet: Color Rendition ISP Net](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.10562)**<br><sub>To match a smartphone ISP's scene-dependent color rendition, combines image metadata with classification-derived global semantics; contributes real and HDR-monitor captures spanning lighting, exposure and gain settings for color-focused ISP evaluation.</sub> | arXiv 2022 | — |
| **[LW-ISP: A Lightweight Model with ISP and Deep Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03904)**<br><sub>To reduce neural-ISP deployment cost, augments a U-Net with fine-grained attention and an upsampling block; heterogeneous distillation transfers clean-image features and reconstruction knowledge from a larger teacher into the compact student.</sub> | BMVC 2022 | — |
| **[Transform your Smartphone into a DSLR Camera: Learning the ISP in the Wild](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.10636)**<br><sub>To learn from weakly paired phone/DSLR images, combines a color-conditional ISP, parametric color alignment and a global-context Transformer predictor; a masked alignment loss excludes unreliable motion regions, alongside the new ISPW dataset. <i>Note: Repo currently only offers the ISPW dataset download; README says "Code will be released soon"</i></sub> | ECCV 2022 | [GitHub (coming soon)](https://github.com/4rdhendu/TransformPhone2DSLR) |
| **[CSAnet: High Speed Channel Spatial Attention Network for Mobile ISP](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021W/MAI/html/Hsyu_CSAnet_High_Speed_Channel_Spatial_Attention_Network_for_Mobile_ISP_CVPRW_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To balance RAW-to-RGB fidelity and mobile speed, combines channel attention with spatial attention implemented by dilated depthwise convolution; the simplified attention module reduces inference cost for end-to-end ISP.</sub> | CVPRW (MAI) 2021 | — |
| **[Del-Net: A Single-Stage Network for Mobile Camera ISP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01623)**<br><sub>To avoid sequential ISP error accumulation within a mobile budget, uses a multiscale CNN with spatial/channel attention for global color and lightweight residual attention blocks for denoising, jointly learning the RAW-to-RGB pipeline.</sub> | arXiv 2021 | — |
| **[Deep Camera: A Fully Convolutional Neural Network for Image Signal Processing](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.09191)**<br><sub>To reduce error accumulation in sequential ISP stages, trains a fully convolutional network end to end for defect-pixel correction, denoising, white balance, exposure, demosaicing, color transformation and gamma encoding.</sub> | ICCVW 2019 | — |
| **[DeepISP: Towards Learning an End-to-End Image Processing Pipeline](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.06724)**<br><sub>To learn low-light restoration and rendering together, maps mosaiced RAW through local denoising/demosaicing and global color-adjustment stages; introduces paired low-/normal-light Samsung S7 data for evaluating the complete learned pipeline.</sub> | IEEE TIP 2018 | — |

### RAW Denoising & Noise Modeling

Single-image RAW noise removal, sensor-noise calibration and synthesis, including self-supervised denoising. Brightness/rendering recovery belongs to low-light; temporal fusion belongs to burst or video.

**With pretrained weights (13)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[2-Shots in the Dark: Low-Light Denoising with Minimal Data Acquisition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.03245)**<br><sub>To synthesize camera-specific training noise with minimal capture effort, uses one noisy image and one dark frame per ISO: Poisson sampling models shot noise, while Fourier spectral sampling preserves signal-independent noise's spatial and statistical structure.</sub> | CVPR 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/IVRL/2-Shots-in-the-Dark)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [SID/ELD and LRID models + dark-frame resources (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Hz4rzV8578lHCTzQkwCHE2nrphQy1QYG?usp=sharing) |
| **[Learned Nonlocal Feature Matching and Filtering for RAW Image Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17453)**<br><sub>To retain interpretable self-similarity while learning RAW denoising, builds a nonlocal block performing neighbor matching, collaborative filtering and aggregation over multiscale learned features; integrates the classical patch pipeline into a trainable network.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/MIA-UIB/nonlocal-matchfilter)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [GitHub Releases (with weights)](https://github.com/MIA-UIB/nonlocal-matchfilter/releases) |
| **[Learning Physics-Informed Noise Models from Dark Frames for Low-Light Raw Image Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09126)**<br><sub>To learn sensor noise without clean/noisy pairs, trains a physics-informed neural proxy from dark frames using physics-guided noise decoupling, a physics-aware proxy model and differentiable distribution loss; also releases LRID. <i>Note: Provides PNNP weights for Sony A7S2 and IMX686; the training code for PNNP itself is not open-sourced</i></sub> | IEEE TPAMI 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/fenghansen/PNNP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Checkpoints & Resources (Baidu, code vmcl)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1WMv2x7yqg0kMTBCddqkCLQ?pwd=vmcl)<br>[LRID dataset (Hugging Face)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/hansen97/LRID) |
| **[Learning Joint Denoising, Demosaicing, and Compression from the Raw Natural Image Noise Dataset](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.08924)**<br><sub>To support sensor- and rendering-flexible denoising, releases paired natural RAW images and compares Bayer versus linear-RGB restoration; jointly learning RAW denoising/compression improves rate–distortion efficiency while preserving later editing freedom. <i>Note: Weights are dual-licensed under GPL3 and CC-BY-4.0.</i></sub> | arXiv 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/trougnouf/rawnind_jddc)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pre-trained models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12Uc5sT4OWx02sviUS_boDk1zDSDRVorw?usp=sharing) |
| **[Noise Modeling in One Hour: Minimizing Preparation Efforts for Self-supervised Low-Light RAW Image Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00045)**<br><sub>To reduce camera-specific noise-synthesis preparation, analyzes sensor-noise properties and removes explicit system-gain calibration and signal-independent-noise profiling; constructs synthetic training noise with preparation reduced from days to hours.</sub> | CVPR 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SonyResearch/raw_image_denoising)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained checkpoints (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1KyR9f6SIciXWv29owm0xYPCOnaMd9YWh?usp=sharing) |
| **[YOND: Practical Blind Raw Image Denoising Free from Camera-Specific Data Dependency](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03645)**<br><sub>To denoise unknown cameras without camera-specific training, combines coarse-to-fine noise estimation, expectation-matched variance stabilization and an SNR-guided denoiser; supports both automatic strength adaptation and manual adjustment.</sub> | IEEE TPAMI 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/fenghansen/YOND_public)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [SNR-Net weights + training data (Baidu, code nn4v)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1tAJW_57v2jWJ605MWKMKVg?pwd=nn4v)<br>[Online demo (HF Spaces)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/hansen97/YOND) |
| **[DualDn: Dual-domain Denoising via Differentiable ISP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18783)**<br><sub>To avoid choosing between RAW detail preservation and sRGB perceptual quality, links RAW- and sRGB-domain denoisers through a differentiable ISP; jointly trains both stages and contributes the Real-Captured Camera-Independent Denoising dataset. <i>Note: Both models are trained on MIT-Adobe FiveK with a Restormer backbone; the README table also links test sets and visual results.</i></sub> | ECCV 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/OpenImagingLab/DualDn)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained_model.zip, synthetic test (OneDrive)](https://mycuhk-my.sharepoint.com/:u:/g/personal/1155231343_link_cuhk_edu_hk/Eb2uUHfx8pRBimlrVRbR0dUB5arCuP6Vx5g3LKxImOUv3w?e=XLXLKC)<br>[DualDn_Big.pth, real captures / DND (OneDrive)](https://mycuhk-my.sharepoint.com/:u:/g/personal/1155231343_link_cuhk_edu_hk/EeSssinwPSRLvC2zOTdmAd8BLLtF3MaKfFw2kYv25WthkQ?e=bbO0Ql) |
| **[Make Explicit Calibration Implicit: Calibrate Denoiser Instead of the Noise Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.03448)**<br><sub>To adapt RAW denoisers without explicit sensor-noise calibration, pretrains with virtual cameras and implicitly calibrates the denoiser through few-pair fine-tuning; structural adjustments reduce synthetic-to-real noise mismatch without extra inference cost. <i>Note: Since 2025-12 also includes UltraLED code and data</i></sub> | ICCV 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Srameo/LED)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Models Zoo (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/11MYkjzbPIZ7mJbu9vrgaVC-OwGcOFKsM?usp=sharing)<br>[related files (Baidu, code iay5)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/17rA_8GvfNPZJY5Zl9dyILw?pwd=iay5)<br>[weight table by camera/method](https://github.com/Srameo/LED/blob/main/docs/pretrained-models.md) |
| **[Towards General Low-Light Raw Noise Synthesis and Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.16508)**<br><sub>To capture signal-independent noise beyond simple distributions, combines physical shot-noise synthesis with a learned generative noise model and a multiscale Fourier Transformer discriminator; releases LRD for cross-sensor evaluation. <i>Note: Noise synthesis model not released due to commercial licensing</i></sub> | ICCV 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/fengzhang427/LRD)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [RAW denoising models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VkgHyEU6hNsXLL1vRfFWWLZCmGYGyi_h/view?usp=sharing)<br>[Mirror (Baidu, code ujzm)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1iMNrQh5P4g2prhhk2Tcu_g) |
| **[Pseudo-ISP: Learning Pseudo In-camera Signal Processing Pipeline from A Color Image Denoiser](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.10234)**<br><sub>To adapt sRGB denoisers to unfamiliar sensor/ISP noise, learns a pseudo ISP and RAW noise model from noisy inputs and pseudo-clean outputs, then alternates synthetic-pair generation with denoiser adaptation using unpaired clean images.</sub> | arXiv 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/happycaoyue/Pseudo-ISP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained denoising models (Baidu, code 6aj4)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1W8_Uemrm8coX3wFZ_Jlw1g) |
| **[Rethinking Noise Synthesis and Modeling in Raw Denoising](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2021/html/Zhang_Rethinking_Noise_Synthesis_and_Modeling_in_Raw_Denoising_ICCV_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To avoid inaccurate per-sensor parametric models, samples real sensor noise directly; pattern-aligned patch sampling preserves spatial correlations and high-bit reconstruction recovers quantization-hidden variation for realistic RAW-noise synthesis.</sub> | ICCV 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/zhangyi-3/noise-synthesis)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained (Baidu, code v4dh)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1RMYgubpdKZFO8JUkdTC7vg?pwd=v4dh) |
| **[A Physics-based Noise Formation Model for Extreme Low-light Raw Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12751)**<br><sub>To improve extreme-low-light synthetic training, models CMOS shot, long-tailed read, row and quantization noise with a reproducible calibration procedure; releases a multi-camera dataset to test how realistic synthesis transfers to real captures. <i>Note: TPAMI 2021 extended version (arXiv 2108.02158); also accessible under the repo name Vandermode/NoiseModel</i></sub> | CVPR 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Vandermode/ELD)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [ELD data + pretrained models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QoEhB1P-hNzAc4cRb7RdzyEKktexPVgy?usp=sharing)<br>[Mirror (Baidu, code 0lby)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/11ksugpPH5uyDL-Z6S71Q5g) |
| **[Practical Deep Raw Image Denoising on Mobile Devices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.06935)**<br><sub>To make RAW denoising mobile-friendly across ISO values, calibrates sensor-specific synthetic noise and applies a k-Sigma transform that normalizes noise variation; a compact network then handles a wide gain range with measured smartphone latency.</sub> | ECCV 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/MegEngine/PMRID)<br><sub>PyTorch / MegEngine</sub> | [models/torch_pretrained.ckp + mge_pretrained.ckp (in repo)](https://github.com/MegEngine/PMRID/tree/main/models)<br>[benchmark data (Kaggle mirror; the README also lists OneDrive)](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/1bdc5cd707cfbb3ee842eb3cbfe93495dbba88017d29f295f8edbcb8f8790556) |

**Code only or not released (15)**

| Paper | Venue | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **[GALOSH: Blind, Training-Free Denoising of Raw Bayer and sRGB Images by Parallel-Friendly Local Shrinkage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03768)**<br><sub>To avoid training data and expensive patch search, estimates Poisson–Gaussian noise per image, applies generalized Anscombe stabilization and local Walsh–Hadamard luminance shrinkage, then regresses chrominance from luminance; supports parallel, fixed-point RAW/sRGB denoising. <i>Note: Training-free method with no network weights; Releases provide a Windows executable.</i></sub> | arXiv 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/luxgrain/GALOSH)<br><sub>C++ / Python</sub> |
| **[SeNM-VAE: Semi-Supervised Noise Modeling with Hierarchical Variational Autoencoder](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024/html/Zheng_SeNM-VAE_Semi-Supervised_Noise_Modeling_with_Hierarchical_Variational_Autoencoder_CVPR_2024_paper.html)**<br><sub>To learn noise with limited paired data, uses a variational graphical model of clean/degraded conditional distributions and an objective combining paired/unpaired samples; synthesizes training pairs for denoising and super-resolution.</sub> | CVPR 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/zhengdihan/SeNM-VAE)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Physics-Guided ISO-Dependent Sensor Noise Modeling for Extreme Low-Light Photography](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023/html/Cao_Physics-Guided_ISO-Dependent_Sensor_Noise_Modeling_for_Extreme_Low-Light_Photography_CVPR_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To model complex noise across ISO settings, builds a normalizing flow with components guided by physical noise sources and ISO dependence; releases paired images, flat fields and bias frames for training and evaluation. <i>Note: Repo is mainly for the dataset</i></sub> | CVPR 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/happycaoyue/LLD) |
| **[Learnability Enhancement for Low-light Raw Denoising: Where Paired Real Data Meets Noise Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.06103)**<br><sub>To improve learnability of limited real pairs, decouples sensor noise, augments the shot-noise component and corrects dark shading; increases training variation while simplifying the mapping the denoiser must learn. <i>Note: README provides ISO noise parameters and data; pretrained weights are in the later PNNP / LRID release</i></sub> | ACM MM 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/megvii-research/PMN)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Noise2NoiseFlow: Realistic Camera Noise Modeling without Clean Images](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022/html/Maleky_Noise2NoiseFlow_Realistic_Camera_Noise_Modeling_Without_Clean_Images_CVPR_2022_paper.html)**<br><sub>To learn realistic noise without clean references, jointly trains a Noise Flow normalizing-flow model and a denoiser using only noisy/noisy pairs; enables both noise synthesis and denoising under weak supervision.</sub> | CVPR 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SamsungLabs/Noise2NoiseFlow)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Learning Camera-Aware Noise Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.09370)**<br><sub>To model noise more flexibly than fixed sensor distributions, trains a camera-aware generative adversarial noise model from real measurements; one model synthesizes distinct noise characteristics for multiple cameras and gain settings. <i>Note: The checkpoint folder (Google Drive) linked in the README returns 404 (checked 2026-10-11).</i></sub> | ECCV 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/arcchang1236/CA-NoiseGAN)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Learning Raw Image Denoising with Bayer Pattern Unification and Bayer Preserving Augmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.12945)**<br><sub>To train one denoiser across Bayer patterns without invalid RGB-style augmentations, combines BayerUnify pattern normalization and Bayer-preserving augmentation with a modified U-Net, allowing heterogeneous RAW datasets to be pooled safely. <i>Note: Repo contains only the BayerUnify/Aug utility functions</i></sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2019 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Jiaming-Liu/BayerUnifyAug) |
| **[Noise Flow: Noise Modeling with Conditional Normalizing Flows](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.08453)**<br><sub>To express real noise beyond Gaussian approximations, combines conditional normalizing flows with physical signal-dependent noise components; a compact model learns camera/gain-conditioned noise distributions for density estimation and synthesis. <i>Note: Automatically downloads SIDD_Medium_Raw; no separate weight link found</i></sub> | ICCV 2019 | [GitHub](https://github.com/BorealisAI/noise_flow)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> |
| **[A High-Quality Denoising Dataset for Smartphone Cameras](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_cvpr_2018/html/Abdelhamed_A_High-Quality_Denoising_CVPR_2018_paper.html)**<br><sub>To benchmark real smartphone denoising with reliable references, develops a systematic clean-ground-truth estimation procedure and collects about 30,000 noisy images from five phones and ten scenes; supplies RAW/sRGB evaluation data. <i>Note: The repo contains the ground-truth estimation code; the dataset is on the SIDD website</i></sub> | CVPR 2018 | [GitHub](https://github.com/AbdoKamel/sidd-ground-truth-image-estimation) |
| **[RPG-VST: Robust Poisson-Gaussian Variance Stabilization for Blind RAW Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24291)**<br><sub>To stabilize blind noise calibration under outliers, fits per-CFA Poisson–Gaussian parameters with a constrained Student-t log-variance objective; a stabilized-noise reliability test selects robust or least-squares fitting before a frozen Gaussian denoiser.</sub> | IEEE SPL 2026 | — |
| **[Why Low-Light Cameras Go Color Blind: Removing Color Bias in Raw Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11090)**<br><sub>To address cross-camera color shifts in blind low-light denoising, identifies black-level estimation error as a key bias source and predicts it with a global bias-estimator network, reducing dependence on camera-specific calibration.</sub> | ICCP 2026 | — |
| **[Non-parametric Sensor Noise Modeling and Synthesis](https://www.ecva.net/papers/eccv_2024/papers_ECCV/html/3438_ECCV_2024_paper.php)**<br><sub>To avoid restrictive sensor-noise distributions, estimates intensity-dependent probability mass functions directly from captures and interpolates across ISO; also synthesizes additional noise when only already-noisy images are available.</sub> | ECCV 2024 | — |
| **[Contrastive Learning for Low-light Raw Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.03352)**<br><sub>To preserve weak high-frequency details under extreme noise, introduces denoising contrastive regularization that pulls restored features toward clean images and away from noisy inputs; a Wnet embedding extracts high-frequency cues.</sub> | AAAI 2023 | — |
| **[ELMformer: Efficient Raw Image Restoration with a Locally Multiplicative Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.14704)**<br><sub>To restore single-channel RAW efficiently, combines bidirectional fusion projection for spatial/color structure with locally multiplicative self-attention; the Transformer reduces attention cost while supporting both RAW denoising and deblurring. <i>Note: Repo contains only a README</i></sub> | ACM MM 2022 | [GitHub (coming soon)](https://github.com/leonmakise/ELMformer) |
| **[NODE: Extreme Low Light Raw Image Denoising using a Noise Decomposition Network](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.05249)**<br><sub>To handle noise sources amplified in extreme low light, uses a multitask RAW-domain neural network that explicitly estimates defective-pixel noise alongside Gaussian read noise and Poisson shot noise before reconstructing the clean signal.</sub> | arXiv 2019 | — |

### Low-Light Rendering & Exposure Correction

Low-light RAW rendering and exposure correction, including interpretable conventional baselines. RAW-only noise estimation stays under denoising; multi-frame fusion and temporally evaluated methods stay under burst or video.

**With pretrained weights (11)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Hierarchical Mixing Architecture for Low-light RAW Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15497)**<br><sub>To balance low-light quality and efficiency, mixes channel attention and Mamba in hierarchical large/small-scale blocks; local distribution adjustment learns regional luminance/contrast statistics, while multiprior fusion maintains domain-consistent features.</sub> | arXiv 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Cynicarlos/HiMA)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/196hPm0aLqpgsxLryKqKpE0UKgvXE_0ap?usp=drive_link)<br>[pretrained (Baidu, code 8fem)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/146zs6nfFdNcTmA3ytsd7vQ?pwd=8fem) |
| **[LDM-ISP: Enhancing Neural ISP for Low Light with Latent Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.01027)**<br><sub>To reuse pretrained diffusion priors for extremely dark RAW, trains lightweight modules that modulate U-Net features with RAW cues; separates low-frequency latent generation from high-frequency preservation during decoding. <i>Note: Authors state the released model is a retrained version that scores slightly higher than the paper</i></sub> | ICRA 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/csqiangwen/LDM-ISP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained_models (OneDrive/SharePoint)](https://hkustconnect-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/qwenab_connect_ust_hk/EglycxTmf0RNqWc5C3uvRRcBGISUNq2rsOiOqx_fT23Scg?e=kb1BNY) |
| **[Learning to See in the Extremely Dark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21132)**<br><sub>To study illumination down to 0.0001 lux, synthesizes calibrated paired RAW/sRGB data at three light ranges; a diffusion enhancer with adaptive illumination correction and color-consistency loss addresses extreme-noise exposure and color recovery.</sub> | ICCV 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/JianghaiSCU/SIED)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pre-trained model (OneDrive)](https://1drv.ms/f/c/e379fe7c770e3033/Ekg7dQ-J7PxCuJ3_-FQ_uNsB0ZWvwL2HUK3dSFcogki0jA?e=XWToVn)<br>[Mirror (Baidu, code m9zp)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1m3pP50qopY8TRoGwt6wrjA) |
| **[Retinex-RAWMamba: Bridging Demosaicing and Denoising for Low-Light RAW Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07040)**<br><sub>To jointly handle RAW noise, demosaicing and nonlinear exposure, introduces a CFA-aware Mamba architecture and a Retinex decomposition module; decouples illumination and reflectance to reduce reliance on manually chosen linear amplification. <i>Note: Each checkpoint also has a Baidu mirror</i></sub> | IEEE TCSVT 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Cynicarlos/RetinexRawMamba)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Sony (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1eAgm5HHDH0CBUsl-czZ7Kdues3tAPy7W/view?usp=drive_link)<br>[Fuji (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1C9x-VcHdkFt-7MQONSkZAWtttu3Gtp12/view?usp=drive_link)<br>[MCR (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OOuyC7PcODPrcNm1uXx2CZwIS8mchtj7/view?usp=drive_link) |
| **[DNF: Decouple and Feedback Network for Seeing in the Dark](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023/html/Jin_DNF_Decouple_and_Feedback_Network_for_Seeing_in_the_Dark_CVPR_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To resolve ambiguity between noise removal and color mapping, decouples RAW-domain denoising from sRGB reconstruction and feeds features back across stages; avoids information loss caused by passing only intermediate images.</sub> | CVPR 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Srameo/DNF)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [SID Sony (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FHreF_UHFutkiQ0LMdWjX2fahznka0Cb/view?usp=share_link)<br>[SID Fuji (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1WfwZLBbj0EUf_QTYS8Qq5Rzk2iV8QKQ7/view?usp=share_link)<br>[MCR (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kFYnqJTYfYkRWcojGxgV9DpVup4uFFBR/view?usp=share_link)<br>[SID Sony (Baidu, code eoiz)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1-r29zUvCS-Wa2wEYovX89g?pwd=eoiz) |
| **[ExposureDiffusion: Learning to Expose for Low-light Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07710)**<br><sub>To avoid starting enhancement from pure noise, embeds a physical exposure process into diffusion and iteratively restores the noisy input; an adaptive residual layer suppresses overcorrection once regions become well exposed. <i>Note: Same author as R2LCM</i></sub> | ICCV 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/wyf0912/ExposureDiffusion)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [SID_Pg / SID_PGru / SID_real etc. (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qdxZBg-GsYxHaDj3Zd_NikYiweqDOFzo?usp=drive_link) |
| **[Abandoning the Bayer-Filter to See in the Dark](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022/html/Dong_Abandoning_the_Bayer-Filter_To_See_in_the_Dark_CVPR_2022_paper.html)**<br><sub>To exploit monochrome sensitivity without a second sensor at inference, learns a De-Bayer-Filter simulator and fuses synthesized monochrome with color RAW using channel attention; contributes real monochrome/color paired MCR data. <i>Note: MCR dataset also available via Baidu (code 22cv)</i></sub> | CVPR 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/TCL-AILab/Abandon_Bayer-Filter_See_in_the_Dark)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [MCR_pretrained_model (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1GDQxKobmIxw1hn9EToghcBNmKcnT_eJo/view?usp=sharing)<br>[SID_pretrained_model (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1m4Os_EpOQpBbaFXcHbEQA048prMrE8Rl/view?usp=sharing) |
| **[Rendering Nighttime Image Via Cascaded Color and Brightness Compensation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.08970)**<br><sub>To model night illumination explicitly, cascades color- and brightness-compensation networks instead of learning both together; contributes NR2R, a high-resolution night RAW–RGB dataset with expert white-balance and tone annotations. <i>Note: Stage-2 and other weights are listed in the README</i></sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/njuvision/CBUnet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [stage-1 cube++.pth (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1K8CgwXp0Pk7yPNUWXOF6zbK9iHgpiVDS/view?usp=sharing) |
| **[Restoring Extremely Dark Images in Real Time](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/html/Lamba_Restoring_Extremely_Dark_Images_in_Real_Time_CVPR_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To restore dark images with low latency, concentrates computation in coarse scale spaces and processes scales concurrently; an input-only amplifier estimates exposure gain, reducing reliance on externally supplied amplification factors. <i>Note: The repo also includes comparison training scripts for SID / SGN / DID</i></sub> | CVPR 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/MohitLamba94/Restoring-Extremely-Dark-Images-In-Real-Time)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [demo_imgs/weights (in repo, loaded directly by demo.py)](https://github.com/MohitLamba94/Restoring-Extremely-Dark-Images-In-Real-Time/tree/main/demo_imgs) |
| **[EEMEFN: Low-Light Image Enhancement via Edge-Enhanced Multi-Exposure Fusion Network](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v34i07.7013)**<br><sub>To recover detail from a single extremely dark RAW, synthesizes multiple exposure representations, fuses their complementary features and uses edge-enhanced refinement; combines exposure handling and boundary reconstruction in one enhancement framework. <i>Note: Published at AAAI 2020 (no arXiv version)</i></sub> | AAAI 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/MinfengZhu/EEMEFN)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Sony / Fuji models (MEGA)](https://mega.nz/file/uBUhDCaS#sl_3X-ceBsConxcytAH-FUmBfbaO2Zh6e4X3GIVf24w) |
| **[Learning to See in the Dark](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.01934)**<br><sub>To replace failing conventional processing at extreme low SNR, trains a fully convolutional U-Net directly from short-exposure RAW to long-exposure sRGB references; releases paired Sony/Fuji captures establishing a reproducible low-light benchmark. <i>Note: In 2025-09 the authors removed the dataset download script due to storage costs, so data must be downloaded manually; models are still fetched via script</i></sub> | CVPR 2018 | [GitHub](https://github.com/cchen156/Learning-to-See-in-the-Dark)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> | [python download_models.py (script download)](https://github.com/cchen156/Learning-to-See-in-the-Dark#testing) |

|:--|:--|:--|
| **[NEC-Diff: Noise-Robust Event-RAW Complementary Diffusion for Seeing Motion in Extreme Darkness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20005)**<br><sub>To reconstruct motion under severe photon noise, uses a diffusion framework that combines complementary event and RAW measurements; contributes REAL with 47,800 pixel-aligned low-light RAW/event/reference samples spanning 0.001–0.8 lux. <i>Note: Dataset is being uploaded in batches; no weights yet</i></sub> | CVPR 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/jinghan-xu/NEC-Diff) |
| **[ERIENet: An Efficient RAW Image Enhancement Network under Low-Light Environment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.15186)**<br><sub>To accelerate low-light RAW rendering, processes scales in parallel with channel-aware residual dense convolution blocks; a green-channel guidance branch exploits Bayer sampling redundancy to aid reconstruction with lower computational cost. <i>Note: The repo has training/testing code; no weights found.</i></sub> | ICVISP 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/whiteknight-WJN/An-Efficient-RAW-Image-Enhancement-Network-under-Low-Light-Environment)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[TS-Diff: Two-Stage Diffusion Model for Low-Light RAW Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04281)**<br><sub>To adapt diffusion enhancement across cameras, pretrains camera-feature-integration modules on virtual sensors, averages and fine-tunes them on limited target RAW data; a color corrector dynamically aligns global color distributions during diffusion. <i>Note: The pretrained_models/ directory contains only placeholder files</i></sub> | IJCNN 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/CircccleK/TS-Diff)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Day-to-Night Image Synthesis for Training Nighttime Neural ISPs](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022/html/Punnappurath_Day-to-Night_Image_Synthesis_for_Training_Nighttime_Neural_ISPs_CVPR_2022_paper.html)**<br><sub>To reduce expensive nighttime training captures, converts daytime RAW into aligned clean/noisy nighttime pairs with controllable noise; mixing synthetic data with a small real subset trains nighttime neural ISPs. <i>Note: README references pretrained_\* directories, but no weight files were found in the repo and the dataset link is empty</i></sub> | CVPR 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SamsungLabs/day-to-night)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Deep-FlexISP: A Three-Stage Framework for Night Photography Rendering](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022W/NTIRE/html/Liu_Deep-FlexISP_A_Three-Stage_Framework_for_Night_Photography_Rendering_CVPRW_2022_paper.html)**<br><sub>To decouple night-rendering noise, color and brightness, cascades RAW denoising, white balance and Bayer-to-sRGB subnetworks; weakly coupled stages simplify training and allow style adjustments through the intermediate pipeline. <i>Note: The Docker image with the 2022 models (Google Drive) returns 404 (checked 2026-10-11); the repo's Night_Photography_2023 folder ships checkpoints for the team's 2023 challenge entry instead.</i></sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/q935970314/Deep-FlexISP) |
| **[Towards Fast and Light-Weight Restoration of Dark Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.14133)**<br><sub>To accelerate dark-image restoration, packs features into low-resolution representations for most computation and unpacks the output; estimates amplification from the input, reducing both inference cost and manual exposure configuration.</sub> | BMVC 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/MohitLamba94/LLPackNet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Beyond Pixel Fidelity: Minimizing Perceptual Distortion and Color Bias in Night Photography Rendering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.28136)**<br><sub>To reduce night-rendering color bias and perceptual artifacts, pHVI-ISPNet combines HVI-space processing, RAW features and wavelet propagation with exposure-dependent loss weights and a feature-distribution color-constancy loss.</sub> | ICIP 2026 | — |
| **[CtrlISP: Rescuing Low-Light RAW Images via Controllable Neural ISP](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2026F/html/Zhang_CtrlISP_Rescuing_Low-Light_RAW_Images_via_Controllable_Neural_ISP_CVPRF_2026_paper.html)**<br><sub>To make extreme-low-light enhancement user-controllable, cascades differentiable ISP modules: DenoiseNet uses spatial interaction and guidance against dark-shading noise, while ColorNet predicts rendering parameters for adaptive color, brightness and style adjustment.</sub> | CVPR Findings 2026 | — |
| **[Unified RAW Image Exposure Correction and Restoration via Linear Illumination and Frequency-Adaptive Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28191)**<br><sub>To restore both under- and overexposed RAW, predicts channel-aware linear gains with LICN and applies a dual-branch frequency network with dynamic convolution; contributes 1,784 real pairs spanning 223 scenes. <i>Note: Posted 2026-10-20. The author repository labels the work ACAIT 2026 but contains only a README; implementation and weights were not available on 2026-10-28.</i></sub> | arXiv 2026 | [GitHub (coming soon)](https://github.com/yingkai-zhang/RIECR) |
| **[When Extreme Darkness Meets Motion Blur: MeanFlow for Unified RAW Restoration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01720)**<br><sub>To restore jointly dark and motion-blurred RAW, calibrates a shared RAW tokenizer across exposure domains and applies single-evaluation MeanFlow enhancement; physics-guided refinement and the SIDED benchmark address coupled motion/noise degradation.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[DarkDiff: Advancing Low-Light Raw Enhancement by Retasking Diffusion Models for Camera ISP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23743)**<br><sub>To reduce oversmoothing from pixel-regression ISPs, retasks a pretrained generative diffusion model for low-light RAW processing; transfers learned image priors into the camera pipeline to recover perceptually sharper detail and color.</sub> | arXiv 2025 | — |
| **[Physics-Guided Rectified Flow for Low-light RAW Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08330)**<br><sub>To capture spatial sensor-noise variation, combines additive/multiplicative physical noise with per-pixel calibration and synthesis, then trains a physics-guided rectified-flow enhancer; contributes the Sony A7S II indoor LLID benchmark.</sub> | arXiv 2025 | — |
| **[Rethinking Reconstruction and Denoising in the Dark: New Perspective, General Architecture and Beyond](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025/html/Ma_Rethinking_Reconstruction_and_Denoising_in_the_Dark_New_Perspective_General_CVPR_2025_paper.html)**<br><sub>To avoid weak coupling between restoration tasks, shares a chromaticity/noise-aware backbone with compact reconstruction and denoising heads; task-specific supervision and dual-head interaction exchange information beyond image-level cascades.</sub> | CVPR 2025 | — |
| **[Towards Realistic Low-Light Image Enhancement via ISP Driven Data Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.12204)**<br><sub>To synthesize realistic paired low-light data, unprocesses normal-light images to RAW, adds RAW-domain degradations and varies white balance, tone and gamma during re-rendering; validates data effectiveness with a convolutional U-Net baseline.</sub> | arXiv 2025 | — |
| **[Back to the Future: A Night Photography Rendering ISP Without Deep Learning](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023W/NTIRE/html/Zini_Back_to_the_Future_A_Night_Photography_Rendering_ISP_Without_CVPRW_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To avoid night-ISP training-data and compute demands, constructs a shallow, explainable conventional pipeline with few parameters and no learned network; evaluates perceptual rendering through the NTIRE night-photography challenge.</sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2023 | — |
| **[DiffuseRAW: End-to-End Generative RAW Image Processing for Low-Light Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18575)**<br><sub>To use generative priors before lossy ISP processing, fine-tunes a pretrained latent diffusion model directly on low-light RAW to generate long-exposure-like processed images; learns the RAW-to-output pipeline end to end.</sub> | arXiv 2023 | — |
| **[Learning to See Low-Light Images via Feature Domain Adaptation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.06723)**<br><sub>To decouple noise removal and color mapping at single-stage cost, supervises the encoder with clean RAW and adapts features through a line-buffer-friendly Lineformer; removes the RAW supervision branch at inference.</sub> | arXiv 2023 | — |
| **[Progressive Joint Low-light Enhancement and Noise Removal for Raw Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14844)**<br><sub>To adapt joint brightness, color and denoising across cameras with less recollection, combines a coefficient-estimation branch and a joint enhancement/denoising branch; targets camera-specific processing of high-resolution RAW images.</sub> | IEEE TIP 2022 | — |
| **[Shallow Camera Pipeline for Night Photography Rendering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.08972)**<br><sub>To render low-light photographs with few interpretable parameters, uses local light enhancement, global histogram adjustment and stronger denoising in dark regions; the handcrafted pipeline avoids requiring explicit training targets. <i>Note: The paper states code will be released upon acceptance; no repo found.</i></sub> | arXiv 2022 | — |
| **[Towards Low Light Enhancement with RAW Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.14022)**<br><sub>To identify which RAW properties benefit enhancement, introduces a factorized enhancement model for controlled evaluation; REENet learns to exploit RAW during training while supporting sRGB-only input at test time.</sub> | IEEE TIP 2022 | — |
| **[Few-Shot Domain Adaptation for Low Light RAW Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15528)**<br><sub>To transfer low-light enhancement to a new camera, combines labeled source-camera data with ten or fewer labeled target examples through few-shot domain adaptation; contributes paired short/long-exposure Nikon data for cross-camera testing.</sub> | BMVC 2021 | — |
| **[Learning an Adaptive Model for Extreme Low-light Raw Image Processing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.10447)**<br><sub>To avoid manually setting RAW amplification, predicts a scene-dependent target exposure with a brightness-prediction module and renders it through exposure shifting; introduces an image-enhancement vector and Campus Image Dataset for supervision.</sub> | IET Image Processing 2020 | — |
| **[Sky Optimization: Semantically Aware Image Processing of Skies in Low-Light Photography](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPRW_2020/html/w31/Liba_Sky_Optimization_Semantically_Aware_Image_Processing_of_Skies_in_Low-Light_CVPRW_2020_paper.html)**<br><sub>To treat noisy night skies separately, trains a low-resolution sky-segmentation network from partially annotated masks, refines and upsamples masks with a weighted guided filter, then applies sky-specific white balance, tone and noise processing.</sub> | CVPRW 2020 | — |
| **[Learning Digital Camera Pipeline for Extreme Low-Light Imaging](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.05939)**<br><sub>To learn well-exposed rendering from short-exposure RAW, trains a neural camera pipeline with a loss combining pixelwise and perceptual properties; evaluates both numerical fidelity and human visual preference under extreme low light.</sub> | arXiv 2019 | — |

### Demosaicing & Remosaicing

CFA reconstruction and conversion, including joint demosaicing/denoising and Bayer, Quad, Nona or HybridEVS patterns. Dedicated super-resolution and other RAW degradations have separate categories. Burst-based training alone does not imply multi-frame inference.

**With pretrained weights (8)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Binarized Mamba-Transformer for Lightweight Quad Bayer HybridEVS Demosaicing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16134)**<br><sub>To demosaic Quad Bayer HybridEVS efficiently, combines binarized Mamba projections with Swin Transformer blocks while keeping selective scanning full precision; captures global/local dependencies with lower edge-device compute.</sub> | CVPR 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Clausy9/BMTNet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bn7Pxt05H2bJd3MFVB600_UXbkECq9pg/view?usp=sharing) |

| **[DemosaicFormer: Coarse-to-Fine Demosaicing Network for HybridEVS Camera](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07951)**<br><sub>To restore HybridEVS color and defective pixels, cascades coarse demosaicing and pixel correction; a multiscale gating module exchanges features across resolutions for coarse-to-fine reconstruction.</sub> | CVPRW (MIPI) 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/QUEAHREN/DemosaicFormer)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [model (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Fc9LA5KRoprYMlQ8gZmsddKHdDQW0Z8z/view?usp=drive_link) |
| **[Joint Demosaicking and Denoising Benefits from a Two-stage Training Strategy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.06205)**<br><sub>To preserve observed CFA values and stabilize learning, first trains a traditional-plus-residual-CNN demosaicer on clean data, then trains a second CNN on demosaiced noise; compares this staged strategy with joint end-to-end training.</sub> | J. Math. 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Yuguo-math/JDMDN-TwoStage)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Demosaic/{lightweight,normal}.pkl + Denoise/ (in repo)](https://github.com/Yuguo-math/JDMDN-TwoStage) |
| **[CDLNet: Noise-Adaptive Convolutional Dictionary Learning Network for Blind Denoising and Demosaicing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.00913)**<br><sub>To retain interpretability and noise adaptation, unfolds convolutional dictionary learning into a trainable network for denoising and joint demosaicing; evaluates small/large models and unsupervised training.</sub> | IEEE OJSP 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/nikopj/CDLNet-OJSP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [trained_nets/{CDLNet-s2030, JDD_CDLNet-s0120} (in repo)](https://github.com/nikopj/CDLNet-OJSP/tree/HEAD/trained_nets) |

| **[Efficient Deep Demosaicing with Spatially Downsampled Isotropic Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00703)**<br><sub>To reduce demosaicing cost, spatially downsamples before an isotropic fully convolutional network designed with mathematical architecture search; evaluates the efficiency/quality trade-off on demosaicing and joint denoising tasks.</sub> | WACVW 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/cory-fan/jd3net)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |

| **[SAGAN: Adversarial Spatial-asymmetric Attention for Noisy Nona-Bayer Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.08619)**<br><sub>To suppress Nona-Bayer reconstruction artifacts, combines spatial-asymmetric attention for bidirectional transformation and large-kernel global context with adversarial learning; jointly denoises and reconstructs full-color output.</sub> | BMVC 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/sharif-apu/SAGAN_BMVC21)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Deep Joint Demosaicking and Denoising](https://groups.csail.mit.edu/graphics/demosaicnet/)**<br><sub>To train robust joint denoising/demosaicing, mines difficult reconstruction examples at scale and learns a convolutional model from noisy mosaics; supports both Bayer and X-Trans sensor layouts. <i>Note: The PyTorch version does not implement the noise-aware model; see the older Caffe repo mgharbi/demosaicnet_caffe.</i></sub> | SIGGRAPH Asia (TOG) 2016 | [GitHub](https://github.com/mgharbi/demosaicnet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[An Extensible and Lightweight Unified Architecture for Demosaicing Pixel-bin Image Sensors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13136)**<br><sub>To avoid separate networks for each pixel-bin CFA, uses a modular lightweight shared demosaicing architecture and a training-free CFA identifier; supports extensible handling of Quad, Nona and related sensor layouts.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[SegDem: Segmentation helps Demosaicing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07916)**<br><sub>To transfer scene structure into demosaicing, pretrains region/boundary representations with instance segmentation and transfers the decoder to RAW reconstruction; evaluates this strategy with CNN, Transformer and state-space backbones across Single/Quad Bayer.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[Structural Guidance for Unified Joint Demosaicing and Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09995)**<br><sub>To guide noisy sparse-CFA restoration with pretrained structure, encodes mosaic, CFA masks and noise level as a unified observation; a trainable adapter bridges domains before residual fusion of structural and restoration features.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[Lightweight Quad Bayer HybridEVS Demosaicing via State Space Augmented Cross-Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06058)**<br><sub>To separate event-pixel holes from demosaicing, TSANet first inpaints then reconstructs color; a Cross-Swin State Block combines positional priors, cross-attention and linear-complexity state-space modeling for lightweight HybridEVS processing.</sub> | arXiv 2025 | — |
| **[How to Best Combine Demosaicing and Denoising?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.06684)**<br><sub>To determine low-complexity restoration order, analyzes demosaiced-noise statistics and compares staged pipelines; recommends adapted post-demosaic denoising at moderate noise and partial pre-denoising plus a second denoiser at high noise.</sub> | Inverse Probl. Imaging 2024 | — |
| **[Efficient Unified Demosaicing for Bayer and Non-Bayer Patterned Image Sensors](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2023/html/Lee_Efficient_Unified_Demosaicing_for_Bayer_and_Non-Bayer_Patterned_Image_Sensors_ICCV_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To share demosaicing across Bayer and non-Bayer sensors, KLAP adapts only a small set of CFA-specific filters; its inference-time meta-learning variant addresses unknown artifacts in real sensor data.</sub> | ICCV 2023 | — |
| **[Inheriting Bayer's Legacy: Joint Remosaicing and Denoising for Quad Bayer Image Sensor](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13571)**<br><sub>To reuse Bayer ISPs with Quad Bayer sensors, jointly remosaics and denoises without resolution loss using a dual-head network, Swin-based denoising and wavelet processing; hard-patch post-training targets moiré/zipper failures.</sub> | arXiv 2023 | — |
| **[Joint Demosaicing and Denoising with Double Deep Image Priors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09426)**<br><sub>To jointly denoise and demosaic without external training data, optimizes two deep-image-prior networks on a single RAW observation; evaluates reconstruction across multiple noise types and intensities.</sub> | arXiv 2023 | — |
| **[SDAT: Sub-Dataset Alternation Training for Improved Image Demosaicing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15792)**<br><sub>To reduce demosaicing dataset bias without changing architecture, partitions training data into differently biased subsets and alternates them during optimization; evaluates the protocol across several reconstruction backbones.</sub> | IEEE OJSP 2023 | — |
| **[Toward Moiré-Free and Detail-Preserving Demosaicking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.08585)**<br><sub>To reduce moiré without oversmoothing detail, separates spectral and spatial feature aggregation; strengthens global cross-color communication while retaining local spatial contrast for demosaicing and joint denoising.</sub> | arXiv 2023 | — |
| **[StereoISP: Rethinking Image Signal Processing for Dual Camera Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.07390)**<br><sub>To exploit a dual-camera system's additional measurements, uses inter-view disparity to combine stereo RAW inputs for joint denoising and demosaicing; evaluates the preliminary pipeline on synthesized stereo RAW pairs.</sub> | arXiv 2022 | — |
| **[Deep Joint Demosaicing and High Dynamic Range Imaging within a Single Shot](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07281)**<br><sub>To recover full-color HDR from sparse spatially varying exposures, uses spatially varying convolution for Bayer structure and exposure guidance against clipped/dark pixels; jointly optimizes demosaicing and single-shot HDR reconstruction.</sub> | arXiv 2021 | — |
| **[Joint Demosaicking and Denoising in the Wild: The Case of Training Under Ground Truth Uncertainty](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04442)**<br><sub>To train despite imperfect clean targets, models ground-truth uncertainty with a two-stage probabilistic degradation and conjugate prior, optimizing an ELBO; a weak-prior fine-tuning scheme improves out-of-distribution joint restoration.</sub> | AAAI 2021 | — |
| **[Learning to Jointly Deblur, Demosaick and Denoise Raw Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.06459)**<br><sub>To avoid separate-stage artifacts with known blur, introduces an interpretable joint demosaicing/deblurring module and trains on realistically unprocessed RAW; also corrects color-dependent optical point-spread blur in real captures.</sub> | arXiv 2021 | — |
| **[A Review of an Old Dilemma: Demosaicking First, or Denoising First?](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPRW_2020/html/w31/Jin_A_Review_of_an_Old_Dilemma_Demosaicking_First_or_Denoising_CVPRW_2020_paper.html)**<br><sub>To resolve restoration-order choices, reviews and benchmarks noisy-mosaic pipelines and analyzes demosaiced noise; specifies how classic denoisers must be adapted when demosaicing precedes denoising.</sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2020 | — |
| **[Joint Demosaicing and Denoising with Self Guidance](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2020/html/Liu_Joint_Demosaicing_and_Denoising_With_Self_Guidance_CVPR_2020_paper.html)**<br><sub>To exploit Bayer's denser green sampling, first estimates green and uses it to guide missing-color recovery; density-map guidance handles varying spatial frequencies and extends joint restoration to super-resolution. <i>Note: The repo README contains only a TODO; code not released</i></sub> | CVPR 2020 | [GitHub (coming soon)](https://github.com/laulampaul/sgnet) |
| **[Deep Demosaicing for Edge Implementation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.00775)**<br><sub>To reduce edge-device demosaicing cost while controlling zipper/false-color artifacts, develops a compact deep reconstruction model and analyzes artifact formation; evaluates reconstruction accuracy against computational requirements.</sub> | ICIAR 2019 | — |
| **[Joint Demosaicking and Denoising by Fine-Tuning of Bursts of Raw Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.05092)**<br><sub>To bridge synthetic-training and real-sensor noise, learns joint demosaicing/denoising directly from mosaicked bursts without RGB truth; burst-specific self-supervised fine-tuning adapts the CNN to each capture.</sub> | ICCV 2019 | — |
| **[Deep Image Demosaicking using a Cascade of Convolutional Residual Denoising Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.05215)**<br><sub>To make joint restoration interpretable and data-efficient, unrolls a regularized optimization process into cascaded convolutional residual denoisers; learns the prior while retaining an explicit iterative demosaicing structure.</sub> | ECCV 2018 | — |
| **[Learning Deep Convolutional Networks for Demosaicing](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03769)**<br><sub>To learn reconstruction for flexible CFA layouts, trains deep CNN demosaicers and jointly optimizes CFA design with reconstruction; extends evaluation to spatially varying exposure/color for single-shot HDR.</sub> | arXiv 2018 | — |

### RAW Deblurring & Other Restoration

RAW deblurring, deraining, reflection/moiré removal, under-display restoration and general mixed-degradation restoration. Excludes methods whose main objective is demosaicing, denoising or super-resolution.

**With pretrained weights (3)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[DSDNet: Raw Domain Demoiréing via Dual Color-Space Synergy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15756)**<br><sub>To remove moiré while preserving color, fuses RAW and YCbCr streams with dynamically modulated synergic attention; a luminance–chrominance adaptive Transformer separates brightness and color representations for more targeted correction.</sub> | ACM MM 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/xxxxxxxxDSDNet/DSDNet-official)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pre-train models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1hjJLFLX4pvBUxhPIvk6XCvCBLZNQIZ7N?usp=drive_link)<br>[Mirror (Baidu, code ewnv)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/14_hywe6NE320qwFjwMJ31A) |
| **[Image Demoireing in RAW and sRGB Domains](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.09063)**<br><sub>To exploit complementary moiré cues, jointly processes RAW and sRGB using gated-feedback and frequency-selection skip modules; an RGB-guided learned ISP restores camera-dependent color after feature-level demoiréing.</sub> | ECCV 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/rebeccaeexu/RRID)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pre-trained model (Dropbox)](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/wxhxlj6y064fbx4lrotcd/APoEwRwRT82LnW8wzDqvW24?rlkey=ghf505sfpkr8y9z5psourzpk6&st=enbcm5va&dl=0) |
| **[Panel-Specific Degradation Representation for Raw Under-Display Camera Image Restoration](https://www.ecva.net/papers/eccv_2024/papers_ECCV/html/6479_ECCV_2024_paper.php)**<br><sub>To account for panel-dependent under-display degradation, learns implicit OLED-panel representations with unsupervised triplet loss and conditions an efficient restoration Transformer on them; contributes aligned sensor-level real UDC captures.</sub> | ECCV 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/OBAKSA/DREUDC)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Dataset + pretrained models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1k4RQQJhNNKa3J_XC0lI2XGojL8xWCUA9?usp=sharing) |

**Code only or not released (11)**

| Paper | Venue | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Efficient RAW Image Deblurring with Adaptive Frequency Modulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24407)**<br><sub>To deblur RAW efficiently, processes frequency-domain features and adaptively modulates components by spectral position; targets RAW-to-RAW restoration while allowing the same design to extend to sRGB deblurring. <i>Note: The README asks for pretrained models to be placed in checkpoints but gives no download link</i></sub> | arXiv 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/WenlongJiao/FrENet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Toward Efficient Deep Blind Raw Image Restoration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18204)**<br><sub>To generalize blind restoration across cameras, simulates realistic sensor noise, motion blur and camera shake in RAW and trains on multiple sensors; restores detail before nonlinear ISP processing complicates the degradations.</sub> | ICIP 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/mv-lab/AISP) |
| **[R3: Reconstruction, Raw, and Rain: Deraining Directly in the Bayer Domain](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.24022)**<br><sub>To avoid irreversible ISP mixing during deraining, reconstructs directly from Bayer mosaics before rendering; introduces matched-bit-depth RAW/sRGB rainy captures and a color-invariant Information Conservation Score for evaluation.</sub> | WACV 2026 | — |
| **[RDDM: Practicing RAW Domain Diffusion Model for Real-world Image Restoration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.19154)**<br><sub>To transfer diffusion restoration across RAW distributions, introduces a RAW VAE mapping into enhanced linear images and configurable multi-Bayer LoRA; a scalable sRGB-to-RAW synthesis pipeline supplies low/high-quality training pairs. <i>Note: The repo currently contains only a README and images</i></sub> | arXiv 2025 | [GitHub (coming soon)](https://github.com/YanCHEN-fr/RDDM) |
| **[Removing Reflections from RAW Photos](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025/html/Kee_Removing_Reflections_from_RAW_Photos_CVPR_2025_paper.html)**<br><sub>To separate real reflections using linear image formation, trains on photometrically/geometrically simulated RAW mixtures with optional opposite-view context; a low-resolution separation model and learned upsampler reconstruct full-resolution layers.</sub> | CVPR 2025 | — |
| **[Training Neural Networks on RAW and HDR Images for Restoration Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03640)**<br><sub>To choose effective training representations for high-dynamic-range signals, compares linear-space losses with PQ, PU21 and μ-law display encodings across denoising, deblurring and SR; identifies the benefit of perceptually uniform encodings.</sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2025 | — |
| **[Learning Degradation-Independent Representations for Camera ISP Pipelines](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024/html/Guo_Learning_Degradation-Independent_Representations_for_Camera_ISP_Pipelines_CVPR_2024_paper.html)**<br><sub>To generalize across compounded sensor and ISP degradations, refines a self-supervised baseline into degradation-independent representations; the learned features transfer to blind restoration, detection and instance segmentation under unfamiliar imaging conditions.</sub> | CVPR 2024 | — |
| **[Deep Contrastive Patch-Based Subspace Learning for Camera Image Signal Processing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.00253)**<br><sub>To handle spatially heterogeneous artifacts, PSL-AE contrastively embeds noisy/clean patches into local subspaces and trains cluster-specific decoders; replaces a uniform full-image filter with patch-dependent reconstruction.</sub> | IEEE AIC 2023 | — |
| **[End-to-end Rain Streak Removal with RAW Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13304)**<br><sub>To avoid ISP information loss before deraining, jointly learns rain removal and RAW processing; synthesizes rain streaks in RAW space and tests transfer across cameras and rendering pipelines.</sub> | arXiv 2023 | — |
| **[ISP-Agnostic Image Reconstruction for Under-Display Cameras](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.01511)**<br><sub>To restore under-display images without fixing their appearance, operates before the legacy ISP and preserves its rendering freedom; uses an HDR-monitor capture/augmentation protocol to obtain diverse high-contrast real training data.</sub> | arXiv 2021 | — |
| **[Raw Image Deblurring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.04264)**<br><sub>To study deblurring before nonlinear rendering, introduces paired RAW/processed Deblur-RAW data and a RAW-oriented restoration network; evaluates sensor transfer and the benefit of RAW training for existing models.</sub> | IEEE TMM 2020 | — |

### RAW Super-Resolution & Resampling

Single-image RAW super-resolution, realistic degradation models and learned RAW downscaling. Joint demosaicing/SR belongs here when resolution scaling is central; multi-frame SR belongs to burst or video.

**With pretrained weights (2)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[End-to-End Learning for Joint Image Demosaicing, Denoising and Super-Resolution](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/html/Xing_End-to-End_Learning_for_Joint_Image_Demosaicing_Denoising_and_Super-Resolution_CVPR_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To avoid accumulated errors across three restoration stages, trains a single CNN jointly for denoising, demosaicing and super-resolution; compares task combinations and losses, including mean absolute error supervision.</sub> | CVPR 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/xingwz/End-to-End-JDNDMSR)<br><sub>Keras</sub> | [models/jdndmsr+_model.h5 etc. (in repo)](https://github.com/xingwz/End-to-End-JDNDMSR/tree/main/models) |
| **[Deep Residual Network for Joint Demosaicing and Super-Resolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.06573)**<br><sub>To avoid amplifying demosaicing artifacts during upscaling, trains a residual CNN directly from low-resolution Bayer mosaics to high-resolution RGB; jointly solves missing colors and spatial detail in one step. <i>Note: Third-party PyTorch reimplementation.</i></sub> | CIC 2018 | [GitHub (unofficial)](https://github.com/Linwei-Chen/Deep-Residual-Network-for-JointDemosaicing-and-Super-Resolution)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Third-party reimplementation weights (Baidu)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1QtwMmSbTNTfosQ3eEDW2Pg) |

**Code only or not released (9)**

| Paper | Venue | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **[BSRAW: Improving Blind RAW Image Super-Resolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.15487)**<br><sub>To improve blind RAW super-resolution in real scenes, synthesizes sensor noise, defocus and exposure degradations before ISP nonlinearities; trains sensor-domain models and contributes a DSLM dataset for real-capture benchmarking. <i>Note: Code and degradation tools are in mv-lab/AISP (imresutils).</i></sub> | WACV 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/mv-lab/AISP) |
| **[Rethinking Learning-based Demosaicing, Denoising, and Super-Resolution Pipeline](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.02538)**<br><sub>To determine how restoration order affects quality, compares denoising/demosaicing/SR pipelines and embeds intermediate supervision through detachable heads; recommends DN→SR→DM and contributes PixelShift200 for evaluation. <i>Note: The README links to the PixelShift200 and DIV2K data.</i></sub> | ICCP 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/guochengqian/TENet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Towards Real Scene Super-Resolution with Raw Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.12156)**<br><sub>To reduce realistic-degradation mismatch and lost radiance, simulates camera formation for training and uses a dual CNN on RAW; spatially varying color transformation restores local color after super-resolution. <i>Note: The repo contains code for the TPAMI 2021 extended version. The ×2 / ×4 model folders (Google Drive) linked in the README return 404 (checked 2026-10-11).</i></sub> | CVPR 2019 | [GitHub](https://github.com/xuxy09/RawSR)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> |
| **[Zoom to Learn, Learn to Zoom](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.05169)**<br><sub>To train real computational zoom despite imperfect alignment, captures optical-zoom RAW reference pairs in SR-RAW and introduces contextual bilateral loss; trains a deep model robust to small input/target displacements. <i>Note: The README provides the SR-RAW dataset (Google Drive / Baidu, code wi02) and quick inference instructions.</i></sub> | CVPR 2019 | [GitHub](https://github.com/ceciliavision/zoom-learn-zoom)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> |
| **[RAW-Domain Degradation Models for Realistic Smartphone Super-Resolution](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2026/html/Mosleh_RAW-Domain_Degradation_Models_for_Realistic_Smartphone_Super-Resolution_CVPR_2026_paper.html)**<br><sub>To reduce synthetic-to-real SR mismatch, calibrates device-specific blur/noise and unprocesses rendered images into smartphone RAW; trains mosaicked-RAW super-resolution and evaluates real captures from a held-out device.</sub> | CVPR 2026 | — |
| **[Camera-Specific Imaging Simulation for Raw Domain Image Super Resolution](https://doi.org/10.1145/3746027.3754785)**<br><sub>To supply camera-matched RAW SR pairs, accelerates physical simulation through subgraph decomposition; LatentKAN combines stage-supervised iterative feature fusion and learnable Kolmogorov–Arnold activations to reduce spectral bias.</sub> | ACM MM 2025 | — |
| **[Learning Arbitrary-Scale RAW Image Downscaling with Wavelet-based Recurrent Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.23219)**<br><sub>To downscale RAW at arbitrary factors without losing structure, recurrently reconstructs wavelet low/high-frequency bands with separate scaling and prediction modules; adds an energy loss and a real noninteger-scale benchmark. <i>Note: "Code is coming soon".</i></sub> | ACM MM 2025 | [GitHub (coming soon)](https://github.com/RenYangSCU/ASRD) |
| **[RBSFormer: Enhanced Transformer Network for Raw Image Super-Resolution](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024W/NTIRE/html/Jiang_RBSFormer_Enhanced_Transformer_Network_for_Raw_Image_Super-Resolution_CVPRW_2024_paper.html)**<br><sub>To super-resolve RAW before complex ISP artifacts arise, enhances a Transformer with cross-covariance attention and gated feed-forward blocks; RAW augmentation and hybrid ensembling improve reconstruction under a compact parameter budget.</sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2024 | — |
| **[Joint Demosaicing and Super-Resolution (JDSR): Network Design and Perceptual Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.03558)**<br><sub>To combine CFA reconstruction and upscaling perceptually, uses a predemosaicer plus residual-dense squeeze-and-excitation blocks; a relativistic discriminator and pre-excitation perceptual loss improve textured-region reconstruction.</sub> | IEEE TCI 2020 | — |
