### Burst & HDR Imaging

Multi-frame still-image fusion for restoration, super-resolution and HDR, plus single-shot sensor-domain HDR reconstruction. Includes low-light fusion; continuous sequences with temporal output belong to video.

**With pretrained weights (13)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Dynamic Exposure Burst Image Restoration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21784)**<br><sub>To adapt burst acquisition to motion and lighting, BAENet predicts per-frame exposure from a preview, motion and gain; a differentiable burst simulator and staged training jointly optimize capture and restoration.</sub> | CVPR 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/woo525/DEBIR)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Official weights (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/13MfH52gQVCwDvasXscaVnv6zUwokCBJe) |
| **[BurstM: Deep Burst Multi-scale SR using Fourier Space with Optical Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15384)**<br><sub>To support flexible-scale burst SR, estimates optical flow for frame alignment and continuous Fourier coefficients for high-frequency textures; one model reconstructs several output scale factors.</sub> | ECCV 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Egkang-Luis/BurstM)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [SyntheticBurst models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XzBOV_F2un0nBWBdCCQCmDzvXlmee-cO/view?usp=sharing)<br>[BurstSR models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1id83q_IOF7qawO5_4WJ4ZGOFvxkcwbFw/view?usp=sharing) |
| **[Burstormer: Burst Image Restoration and Enhancement Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.01194)**<br><sub>To exchange information under complex burst motion, uses a Transformer with deformable alignment, reference-feature enrichment and cyclic burst sampling; progressively fuses local/nonlocal context before upsampling. <i>Note: Weights for the other tasks are listed in the subdirectory READMEs.</i></sub> | CVPR 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/akshaydudhane16/Burstormer)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [synthetic burst SR checkpoint (OneDrive)](https://mbzuaiac-my.sharepoint.com/:u:/g/personal/akshay_dudhane_mbzuai_ac_ae/ER8mPnjoSIZAnaKA8YyCeE8BA_uQr_73b5qRZx9sh9Rzvw?e=Sc4HFJ) |
| **[Joint Demosaicing and Deghosting of Time-Varying Exposures for Single-Shot HDR Imaging](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2023/html/Kim_Joint_Demosaicing_and_Deghosting_of_Time-Varying_Exposures_for_Single-Shot_HDR_ICCV_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To combine time-varying Quad-Bayer exposures without ghosting, extracts mosaicked exposure features and registers spatial/color displacements with a multiscale Transformer; contributes matching sensor-pattern data for joint HDR demosaicing.</sub> | ICCV 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/KAIST-VCLAB/singshot-hdr-demosaicing)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained best_psnr_mu.pt (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/19W4kWG1YngX10CCT-f9rn7TdqIIpunjc/view?usp=sharing) |
| **[RawHDR: High Dynamic Range Image Reconstruction from a Single Raw Image](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02020)**<br><sub>To recover HDR from a single RAW, learns hard/easy exposure masks and combines informative-channel intensity guidance with global spatial guidance; contributes paired RAW/HDR data for highlights and shadow reconstruction.</sub> | ICCV 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/yunhao-zou/RawHDR)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained model (OneDrive)](https://1drv.ms/u/c/451f7e5b32aa37e0/EaqD9NpDCCFDlHQ68yWLYFQBsNFXk1fBvWkDWcy6Dq95Gw?e=gqyglJ) |
| **[Towards Real-World Burst Image Super-Resolution: Benchmark and Method](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.04803)**<br><sub>To aggregate real bursts without dense pixelwise alignment, combines homography registration with federated affinity fusion; contributes RealBSR-RAW/RGB data for studying real degradation and complementary interframe detail. <i>Note: The Google Drive copy of the checkpoint returns 404 (checked 2026-10-11).</i></sub> | ICCV 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/yjsunnn/FBANet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [RealBSR checkpoint model_best.pth (Baidu, code f9ew)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1y0OSXD9ExMj4mQ8Sj0VpoA?pwd=f9ew) |
| **[A Differentiable Two-stage Alignment Scheme for Burst Image Reconstruction with Large Shift](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022/html/Guo_A_Differentiable_Two-Stage_Alignment_Scheme_for_Burst_Image_Reconstruction_With_CVPR_2022_paper.html)**<br><sub>To handle large burst shifts efficiently, first performs differentiable progressive block matching at patch level, then refines alignment implicitly in full-resolution features; supports joint burst denoising and demosaicing.</sub> | CVPR 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/GuoShi28/2StageAlign)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [experiments/.../models (in repo)](https://github.com/GuoShi28/2StageAlign/tree/main/experiments/J0007_JDDB_PBMNet_wgr_ncc_gt_s2h/models) |
| **[BSRT: Improving Burst Super-Resolution with Swin Transformer and Flow-Guided Deformable Alignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.08332)**<br><sub>To recover burst detail under motion, combines a Swin Transformer backbone with pyramid flow-guided deformable alignment; models long-range structure while merging complementary textures from accurately aligned RAW frames.</sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Algolzw/BSRT)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [all pretrained weights (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Bv1ZwoE3s8trhG--wjB0Yt6WJIQPpvsn/view?usp=sharing) |
| **[Burst Image Restoration and Enhancement](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022/html/Dudhane_Burst_Image_Restoration_and_Enhancement_CVPR_2022_paper.html)**<br><sub>To fuse complementary burst details while rejecting degradation, aligns features with an edge-boosting module and constructs pseudo-burst representations; adaptive aggregation progressively merges these features and increases resolution. <i>Note: Weights for each subtask are listed in the subdirectory READMEs (Burst_Super_Resolution / Burst De-noising).</i></sub> | CVPR 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/akshaydudhane16/BIPNet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [synthetic burst SR model BIPNet.ckpt (OneDrive)](https://mbzuaiac-my.sharepoint.com/:u:/g/personal/akshay_dudhane_mbzuai_ac_ae/EYlxq0X49fRGiFD3kMxnM6IB7VNtwhd3atNr4oc1b1psbA?e=pLN14I) |
| **[Deep Burst Super-Resolution](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/html/Bhat_Deep_Burst_Super-Resolution_CVPR_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To learn multiframe RAW zoom, aligns noisy frames with optical flow and fuses them with attention before denoised RGB upsampling; contributes BurstSR smartphone bursts paired with DSLR high-resolution references. <i>Note: Challenge toolkit: goutamgmb/NTIRE21_BURSTSR.</i></sub> | CVPR 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/goutamgmb/deep-burst-sr)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Model Zoo (auto-downloaded by install script)](https://github.com/goutamgmb/deep-burst-sr#model-zoo) |
| **[Deep Reparametrization of Multi-Frame Super-Resolution and Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.08286)**<br><sub>To combine physical fusion and learned priors, reparameterizes a multi-frame MAP objective using learned error metrics and latent image features; applies the same latent-space optimization to burst denoising and super-resolution.</sub> | ICCV 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/goutamgmb/deep-rep)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Model Zoo (auto-downloaded by install script)](https://github.com/goutamgmb/deep-rep#model-zoo) |
| **[EBSR: Feature Enhanced Burst Super-Resolution with Deformable Alignment](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021W/NTIRE/html/Luo_EBSR_Feature_Enhanced_Burst_Super-Resolution_With_Deformable_Alignment_CVPRW_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To align and reconstruct burst textures, combines feature-enhanced pyramid deformable alignment, cross-nonlocal fusion and long-range concatenation reconstruction; cascading residual paths improve information flow across stages.</sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Algolzw/EBSR)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Synthetic track model (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_WA2chhITIsCj6qImcEM2lD6c-iJsRpy/view?usp=sharing)<br>[Real track model (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Zz21YwNtiKZCjerrZsdvcWyubqTJBwaD/view?usp=sharing) |
| **[Joint Denoising and Demosaicking with Green Channel Prior for Real-world Burst Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.09870)**<br><sub>To preserve structure in noisy real bursts, uses Bayer's denser and cleaner green channel as a prior for joint denoising/demosaicing; guides missing-color recovery with this more reliable sampled information.</sub> | IEEE TIP 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/GuoShi28/GCP-Net)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [experiments/gcpnet_model/600000_G.pth (in repo)](https://github.com/GuoShi28/GCP-Net/blob/main/experiments/gcpnet_model/600000_G.pth) |

No implementation or pretrained checkpoint link was found in the paper or repository search on 2026-10-28.</i></sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |

| **[QMambaBSR: Burst Image Super-Resolution with Query State Space Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.08665)**<br><sub>To distinguish consistent subpixel detail from random burst noise, combines interframe queries with intraframe state-space scanning; adaptive upsampling predicts kernels from the recovered subpixel distribution for scene-dependent reconstruction.</sub> | CVPR 2025 | — |
| **[CoDISP: Exploring Compressed Domain Camera ISP with RGB-guided Encoder](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024W/MAI/html/Zhang_CoDISP_Exploring_Compressed_Domain_Camera_ISP_with_RGB-guided_Encoder_CVPRW_2024_paper.html)**<br><sub>To reduce high-resolution multi-frame memory traffic, transfers RAW into a learned RGB-compression latent space; performs registration, denoising and demosaicing in that compact domain while retaining semantic and high-frequency information.</sub> | CVPRW (MAI) 2024 | — |
| **[Improving Bracket Image Restoration and Enhancement with Flow-guided Alignment and Enhanced Feature Aggregation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10358)**<br><sub>To align noisy blurred exposures, IREANet guides deformable alignment and spatial attention with optical flow; recurrent enhanced residual aggregation merges aligned features, with Bayer-preserving augmentation for robust RAW training.</sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2024 | — |
| **[Efficient HDR Reconstruction from Real-World Raw Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10311)**<br><sub>To deploy RAW HDR reconstruction efficiently, RepUNet uses structural reparameterization and a motion-alignment loss against ghosting; contributes the RealRaw-HDR data-formation pipeline and real-capture benchmark.</sub> | arXiv 2023 | — |
| **[End-to-End Single-Frame Image Signal Processing for High Dynamic Range Scenes](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/WACV2023/html/Dinh_End-to-End_Single-Frame_Image_Signal_Processing_for_High_Dynamic_Range_Scenes_WACV_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To render shadows and highlights without burst capture, trains a single-frame Bayer ISP against multi-frame-merged targets; multi-head mixtures handle brightness and camera color settings using supervised, unsupervised and adversarial losses.</sub> | WACV 2023 | — |
| **[Gated Multi-Resolution Transfer Network for Burst Restoration and Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06703)**<br><sub>To reconstruct precise detail from degraded bursts, combines multiscale feature alignment, transposed-attention merging and resolution-transfer upsampling; specializes each module for alignment, aggregation and output reconstruction.</sub> | CVPR 2023 | — |
| **[Self-Supervised Burst Super-Resolution](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2023/html/Bhat_Self-Supervised_Burst_Super-Resolution_ICCV_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To train without high-resolution references, uses a learned forward imaging model to supervise reconstruction from only noisy low-resolution bursts; exploits aliased high frequencies and accommodates dynamic motion in real captures.</sub> | ICCV 2023 | — |
| **[High Dynamic Range and Super-Resolution from Raw Image Bursts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.14671)**<br><sub>To reconstruct HDR and resolution together, jointly processes exposure-bracketed handheld RAW bursts rather than cascading separate merging and upscaling stages; exploits spatial and exposure diversity for a high-resolution HDR color output.</sub> | SIGGRAPH (TOG) 2022 | — |
| **[Burst Photography for Learning to Enhance Extremely Dark Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.09845)**<br><sub>To recover detail from extremely dark bursts, first predicts low-resolution clean RAW, then refines textures in a fine network; permutation-invariant feature fusion combines multiple frames without depending on their input order.</sub> | IEEE TIP 2021 | — |
| **[Lucas-Kanade Reloaded: End-to-End Super-Resolution from Raw Image Bursts](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2021/html/Lecouat_Lucas-Kanade_Reloaded_End-to-End_Super-Resolution_From_Raw_Image_Bursts_ICCV_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To align bursts with subpixel precision while retaining physical interpretation, embeds learnable Lucas–Kanade registration and an image prior in an end-to-end RAW reconstruction algorithm; exploits aliasing as super-resolution information.</sub> | ICCV 2021 | — |
| **[Merging-ISP: Multi-Exposure High Dynamic Range Image Signal Processing](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.04762)**<br><sub>To avoid error propagation through independent HDR and ISP stages, jointly learns multi-exposure merging, demosaicing and rendering in one neural pipeline; maps RAW measurements directly to the final HDR image.</sub> | GCPR 2021 | — |
| **[A Decoupled Learning Scheme for Real-world Burst Denoising from Raw Images](https://www.ecva.net/papers/eccv_2020/papers_ECCV/html/4913_ECCV_2020_paper.php)**<br><sub>To avoid entangling motion estimation with sensor noise, designs a multiframe CNN that learns motion and noise statistics separately; evaluates the decoupled fusion scheme on synthetic and real dynamic RAW sequences.</sub> | ECCV 2020 | — |
| **[Burst Denoising via Temporally Shifted Wavelet Transforms](https://www.ecva.net/papers/eccv_2020/papers_ECCV/html/1848_ECCV_2020_paper.php)**<br><sub>To support variable-length burst denoising cheaply, shifts wavelet-derived temporal features; high-frequency bands preserve local detail while low-frequency bands carry structure, trained with realistic sensor noise for deployment.</sub> | ECCV 2020 | — |
| **[Deep Snapshot HDR Imaging Using Multi-Exposure Color Filter Array](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.10232)**<br><sub>To reconstruct HDR from a multi-exposure CFA, jointly learns missing colors and exposure fusion with luminance-normalized inputs/losses; balances errors in bright and dark regions regardless of absolute radiance.</sub> | ACCV 2020 | — |
| **[Low-light Image Restoration with Short- and Long-exposure Raw Pairs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.00199)**<br><sub>To combine sharp but noisy short exposure with clean but blurred long exposure, synthesizes realistic paired RAW degradations and trains LSFNet for alignment-aware fusion; jointly handles motion blur, noise and color distortion.</sub> | arXiv 2020 | — |

### RAW Video

RAW video denoising, enhancement, demoiréing, super-resolution and HDR reconstruction. Temporal output and consistency distinguish video from burst-to-one reconstruction. Task-driven video perception stays under machine vision.

**With pretrained weights (9)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[RViDeformer: Efficient Raw Video Denoising Transformer with a Larger Benchmark Dataset](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00767)**<br><sub>To learn realistic motion-aware denoising efficiently, introduces screen-recaptured ReCRVD data and a Transformer with multibranch spatial/temporal attention across local, downsampled global and neighboring windows; reparameterization reduces inference cost.</sub> | IEEE TCSVT 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/cao-cong/RViDeformer)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [RViDeformer + ISP weights (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HJuJfofg3hsoPB3yHJCkfeel2Uf53ejF?usp=sharing)<br>[Mirror (Baidu, code 4g5b)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/14srTNWoeEgyn7gL2WUpoFQ) |

| **[Unidirectional Video Denoising by Mimicking Backward Recurrent Modules with Look-ahead Forward Ones](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.05532)**<br><sub>To approximate bidirectional context at bounded latency, combines forward recurrence with a look-ahead forward module using near-future frames; forward warping and border enlargement compensate for motion-related missing pixels.</sub> | ECCV 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/nagejacob/FloRNN)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A854tOA6_qB14ax3JZ7bb7tLo0UovkyI?usp=sharing)<br>[pretrained (Baidu, code ogua)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1YomcegvdtoxVPr96odCo8w?pwd=ogua) |
| **[Supervised Raw Video Denoising with a Benchmark Dataset on Dynamic Scenes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.14013)**<br><sub>To obtain dynamic-scene clean/noisy supervision, records controllable motion as repeated static moments for CRVD; separately denoises packed Bayer subsequences using temporal/spatial/channel correlations, then fuses RAW and optionally renders sRGB.</sub> | CVPR 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/cao-cong/RViDeNet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [trained model (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/open?id=1UdP2Pnn6lHeLC6TUN21sq81XyqL3ujNg)<br>[trained model (Baidu, code xssc)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/16nVuu1fGMS0LJqU4z4LAUQ) |
| **[Learning to See Moving Objects in the Dark](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_ICCV_2019/html/Jiang_Learning_to_See_Moving_Objects_in_the_Dark_ICCV_2019_paper.html)**<br><sub>To obtain real supervision for moving low-light scenes, captures synchronized bright/dark videos with an optical splitting system; a fully convolutional model mixing 2D and 3D operations learns RAW-to-RGB spatiotemporal enhancement.</sub> | ICCV 2019 | [GitHub](https://github.com/MichaelHYJiang/Learning-to-See-Moving-Objects-in-the-Dark)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> | [python download_model.py (script download)](https://github.com/MichaelHYJiang/Learning-to-See-Moving-Objects-in-the-Dark) |
| **[Seeing Motion in the Dark](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_ICCV_2019/html/Chen_Seeing_Motion_in_the_Dark_ICCV_2019_paper.html)**<br><sub>To train low-light video without dynamic long-exposure references, uses paired static RAW videos and a siamese network with temporal-stability loss; the learned pipeline generalizes to moving scenes in the released DRV benchmark.</sub> | ICCV 2019 | [GitHub](https://github.com/cchen156/Seeing-Motion-in-the-Dark)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> | [pre-trained model (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1OO97dDJp9GlqijGfcvKpas2PZB0q9o8n?usp=sharing) |

### White Balance & Color Constancy

Illuminant estimation, camera-independent color constancy, mixed lighting and post-capture white-balance editing, including relevant datasets. General color grading, LUT enhancement and tone mapping belong to color/tone.

**With pretrained weights (19)**

| **[Modeling the Lighting in Scenes as Style for Auto White-Balance Correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.09090)**<br><sub>To correct mixed lighting without explicit illuminant estimation, extracts lighting style with multiple heads and predicts spatial blend weights over preset-WB renderings; supports both single- and multi-illuminant scenes. <i>Note: Built on the mixedillWB framework; evaluated on the synthetic mixed-illuminant set of Afifi et al.</i></sub> | WACV 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/birdortyedi/lighting-as-style-awb-correction)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [models/download.py (script download, patch 64 / 128)](https://github.com/birdortyedi/lighting-as-style-awb-correction/blob/master/models/download.py) |

| **[Leveraging the Availability of Two Cameras for Illuminant Estimation](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/html/Abdelhamed_Leveraging_the_Availability_of_Two_Cameras_for_Illuminant_Estimation_CVPR_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To resolve illumination using spectral diversity, feeds measurements from two different camera sensors into a small neural estimator; contributes dual-camera data and compares against heavier single-image methods.</sub> | CVPR 2021 | — |
| **[Multi-color balance for color constancy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.10228)**<br><sub>To correct more than the neutral axis, computes an n-color transform from multiple target/reference color correspondences; adjusts those anchors exactly while extending correction to remaining colors.</sub> | ICIP 2021 | — |

| **[Bag of Color Features For Color Constancy](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.04445)**<br><sub>To estimate illumination with few parameters, pools local color features into a bag representation and reweights them with self-attention; generalizes statistical color-constancy cues without requiring global spatial layout.</sub> | IEEE TIP 2020 | — |
| **[End-to-End Illuminant Estimation Based on Deep Metric Learning](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2020/html/Xu_End-to-End_Illuminant_Estimation_Based_on_Deep_Metric_Learning_CVPR_2020_paper.html)**<br><sub>To make illuminant features less sensitive to scene appearance, trains an illuminant-guided triplet network jointly with regression; groups lighting-consistent samples without a separate illuminant-classification stage.</sub> | CVPR 2020 | — |
| **[Multi-Domain Learning for Accurate and Few-Shot Color Constancy](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2020/html/Xiao_Multi-Domain_Learning_for_Accurate_and_Few-Shot_Color_Constancy_CVPR_2020_paper.html)**<br><sub>To adapt color constancy with few target-camera examples, shares the feature extractor and illuminant estimator across devices while learning camera-specific channel reweighting; updates only those small adaptation parameters for unseen cameras.</sub> | CVPR 2020 | — |

| **[Fast Color Constancy with Patch-wise Bright Pixels](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.07177)**<br><sub>To obtain fast training-free illumination estimates, downsamples into patches and selects a brightness-dependent fraction of bright pixels per patch; applies gray-world statistics only to these selected observations.</sub> | arXiv 2019 | — |

| **[Formulating Camera-Adaptive Color Constancy as a Few-shot Meta-Learning Problem](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.11788)**<br><sub>To adapt quickly to unseen cameras, organizes illuminant regression into physically meaningful color-temperature tasks and meta-learns across cameras; fine-tunes with only a handful of target-device examples.</sub> | arXiv 2018 | — |

| **[Unsupervised Learning for Color Constancy](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.00436)**<br><sub>To avoid calibrated illumination labels, first approximates unknown training illuminants and learns estimator parameters from them; extends the formulation to transfer parameters between sensors using uncalibrated images.</sub> | arXiv 2017 | — |

### Color Correction, Tone & Retouching

Color calibration, color grading, LUTs, tone mapping and photographic retouching. Includes rendered-RGB methods as ISP finishing modules or historical context; these are not full RAW-to-RGB pipelines.

**With pretrained weights (13)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Leveraging Multispectral Sensors for Color Correction in Mobile Cameras](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.08441)**<br><sub>To resolve color ambiguity in RGB sensing, jointly processes high-resolution RGB and auxiliary low-resolution multispectral data in an end-to-end correction model; constructs training/evaluation data from spectral datasets and varied camera sensitivities. <i>Note: Dataset on HF: LucaCogo/MobileSpectralCCDataset</i></sub> | CVPR 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/LucaCogo/Mobile-Spectral-CC)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained/ (in repo, one folder per camera)](https://github.com/LucaCogo/Mobile-Spectral-CC/tree/main/pretrained) |

| **[Lookup Table meets Local Laplacian Filter: Pyramid Reconstruction Network for Tone Mapping](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/b3a08d179347e33414badadf100e4e8d-Abstract-Conference.html)**<br><sub>To tone-map HDR efficiently while retaining local edges, predicts pixelwise basis-LUT weights with a low-resolution Transformer and refines high-frequency pyramid bands using a learned local Laplacian filter; avoids costly high-resolution convolutions. <i>Note: The NeurIPS version is not released due to company policy; only the TPAMI version is released.</i></sub> | NeurIPS 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/fengzhang427/LLF-LUT)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [TPAMI pretrained models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1fkMj0peUbkX2ETC4rCxy0FAL7Gyxgg26/view?usp=sharing)<br>[Mirror (Baidu, code fegh)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1zPkdl0MG6nYNR4ZNC8fqoA?pwd=fegh) |
| **[AdaInt: Learning Adaptive Intervals for 3D Lookup Tables on Real-time Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.13983)**<br><sub>To allocate LUT samples where colors need them, learns nonuniform intervals in 3D color space with a differentiable adaptive-interval transform; adds content-adaptive sampling to existing real-time LUT enhancers.</sub> | CVPR 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/ImCharlesY/AdaInt)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained/AiLUT-\*.pth (in repo)](https://github.com/ImCharlesY/AdaInt/tree/main/pretrained) |
| **[SepLUT: Separable Image-adaptive Lookup Tables for Real-time Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.08351)**<br><sub>To reduce LUT size while retaining color interactions, factors enhancement into component-independent 1D LUTs followed by a component-correlated 3D LUT; learns image-dependent transforms in this separable cascade.</sub> | ECCV 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/ImCharlesY/SepLUT)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained/SepLUT-\*.pth (in repo)](https://github.com/ImCharlesY/SepLUT/tree/main/pretrained) |
| **[Conditional Sequential Modulation for Efficient Global Image Retouching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.10390)**<br><sub>To reproduce pixel-independent retouching efficiently, uses a per-pixel MLP modulated by global condition features; learns global color/tone operations with a compact base network and condition network.</sub> | ECCV 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/hejingwenhejingwen/CSRNet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [experiments/pretrain_models/csrnet.pth (in repo)](https://github.com/hejingwenhejingwen/CSRNet/tree/master/experiments/pretrain_models) |
| **[CURL: Neural Curve Layers for Global Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.13175)**<br><sub>To make learned enhancement interpretable, predicts adjustment curves jointly in RGB, HSV and CIELab with a multicolor-space loss; combines these global neural curve layers with a local multiscale backbone.</sub> | ICPR 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/sjmoran/CURL)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained_models/adobe_dpe (in repo)](https://github.com/sjmoran/CURL) |
| **[DeepLPF: Deep Local Parametric Filters for Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.13985)**<br><sub>To learn spatially local photo adjustments, regresses elliptical, graduated and polynomial filter parameters; applies these interpretable filters selectively instead of relying only on global transforms or unrestricted pixel synthesis.</sub> | CVPR 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/sjmoran/DeepLPF)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained_models/adobe_dpe (in repo)](https://github.com/sjmoran/DeepLPF) |
| **[Learning Image-adaptive 3D Lookup Tables for High Performance Photo Enhancement in Real-time](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.14468)**<br><sub>To enhance high-resolution photos cheaply, jointly learns basis 3D LUTs and a small CNN predicting image-dependent fusion weights; applies the fused transform by lookup rather than dense per-pixel neural processing.</sub> | IEEE TPAMI 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/HuiZeng/Image-Adaptive-3DLUT)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained_models/{sRGB,XYZ} (in repo)](https://github.com/HuiZeng/Image-Adaptive-3DLUT/tree/master/pretrained_models) |
| **[Exposure: A White-Box Photo Post-Processing Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.09602)**<br><sub>To learn a preferred editing style without paired retouches, trains an RL agent to choose interpretable filters and settings with an adversarial objective; reproduces the style distribution of a reference photo collection. <i>Note: Running evaluate.py as described in the README uses the pretrained models</i></sub> | TOG 2018 | [GitHub](https://github.com/yuanming-hu/exposure)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> | [exposure_models releases](https://github.com/yuanming-hu/exposure_models/releases) |
| **[Deep Bilateral Learning for Real-Time Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.02880)**<br><sub>To approximate complex photographic operators on phones, predicts local affine coefficients in a low-resolution bilateral grid and slices them at full resolution; learns content-adaptive transforms from example edits. <i>Note: The google/hdrnet README still points to a pretrained_models folder that is no longer in that repository; the download script is in mgharbi/hdrnet.</i></sub> | SIGGRAPH (TOG) 2017 | [GitHub](https://github.com/google/hdrnet)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> | [pretrained_models/download.py in the original TF repo (script download from MIT CSAIL)](https://github.com/mgharbi/hdrnet/tree/master/pretrained_models) |
| **[DSLR-Quality Photos on Mobile Devices with Deep Convolutional Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.02470)**<br><sub>To bridge phone-to-DSLR appearance differences, trains a residual CNN with content, color and adversarial texture losses on a multi-phone paired dataset; operates on processed photographs rather than RAW sensor measurements.</sub> | ICCV 2017 | [GitHub](https://github.com/aiff22/DPED)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> | [models_orig/{iphone,sony,blackberry}_orig (in repo)](https://github.com/aiff22/DPED/tree/master/models_orig) |

| Paper | Venue | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Adaptive Color Grading](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21169)**<br><sub>To control shadows/highlights independently, predicts tonescale-region thresholds with K-nearest neighbors trained on annotated video frames; region-specific CIELAB adjustments compose into one deployable 3D LUT within an open grading tool. <i>Note: Example training data ships with the repository; the RAW HDR video dataset is to be hosted on the HDRVS page.</i></sub> | CIC 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SamsungLabs/adaptive-color-grading)<br><sub>Python (scikit-learn)</sub> |
| **[FlowTool: Controlling Tool Parameter in Image Retouching via Flow Matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35673)**<br><sub>To predict editable tool settings from images and instructions, models their joint distribution with conditional rectified flow using a vision-language backbone and diffusion Transformer; staged flow training plus reward post-training replaces sequential parameter reasoning.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[Illuminant-Adaptive 3D Lookup Tables for Camera Color Correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11681)**<br><sub>To correct color across spectrally diverse illuminants, conditions nonlinear 3D LUTs on chromaticity-aware illumination features and compresses them with Tucker decomposition; contributes 1,473 illuminant spectra for evaluation. <i>Note: “The code will be released upon acceptance”</i></sub> | arXiv 2026 | [GitHub (coming soon)](https://github.com/claudiom4sir/C2LUT) |
| **[LoopLUT: 3D Lookup Tables with Progressive Region Refinement for Real-Time 4K Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33593)**<br><sub>To add local adaptivity to fast LUT enhancement, cascades a global LUT with region-conditioned residual LUTs; low-resolution gates partition the image so high-resolution rendering needs only a small fixed number of lookups.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |

### Inverse ISP & RAW Synthesis

RGB-to-RAW or linear-color reconstruction, RAW generation and cross-camera RAW translation, including sparse-metadata methods without a central learned coding objective. Learned entropy/rate–distortion methods belong to compression; bidirectional models are classified by their main evaluated contribution.

**With pretrained weights (9)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[RAW-Flow: Advancing RGB-to-RAW Image Reconstruction with Deterministic Latent Flow Matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20364)**<br><sub>To address ambiguous RGB-to-RAW inversion, learns deterministic latent flow matching guided by cross-scale RGB context; a dual-domain autoencoder and feature alignment stabilize transport between RGB and RAW representations.</sub> | AAAI (Oral) 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/liuzhen03/RAW-Flow)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [nikon_d700 / canon_eos_5d weights (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1pUWOdyogxZSumnRCv9HcffCR4sl4Ue60?usp=sharing) |
| **[RawGen: Learning Camera Raw Image Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.00093)**<br><sub>To generate camera-specific linear data with pretrained image priors, adapts diffusion in latent/pixel spaces for text-to-RAW and sRGB inversion; many-to-one inverse-ISP training anchors diverse renderings to the same scene-referred target. <i>Note: The official repo contains no weights and points to the author's repo DY112/RawGen.</i></sub> | arXiv 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SamsungLabs/RawGen)<br><sub>PyTorch (diffusers)</sub> | [kontext_lora.pt + vae_decoder_xyz.pt (Google Drive, author repo DY112/RawGen)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1OkODPg1XDHLRX4-kVDphTtT-CY8CK9-3) |
| **[SpiralDiff: Spiral Diffusion with LoRA for RGB-to-RAW Conversion Across Cameras](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14885)**<br><sub>To handle intensity-dependent inversion difficulty and multiple cameras, uses signal-dependent diffusion weighting plus camera-aware LoRA; adapts a shared RGB-to-RAW model with lightweight sensor-specific parameters. <i>Note: Apache-2.0. The README's model link (huggingface.co/Chuancy/SpiralDiff) returns 404; the checkpoints sit in the dataset repo next to the FiveK DNG data.</i></sub> | CVPR 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Chuancy-TJU/SpiralDiff)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [checkpoints.zip (Hugging Face dataset repo)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Chuancy/SpiralDiff/blob/main/checkpoints.zip) |
| **[Overexposure Mask Fusion: Generalizable Reverse ISP Multi-Step Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11511)**<br><sub>To recover RAW from clipped RGB more reliably, predicts demosaiced RAW rather than Bayer and applies overexposure-mask-guided multistep refinement; permits perceptual supervision and reuse with other reconstruction backbones.</sub> | ECCVW (AIM) 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SenseBrainTech/overexposure-mask-reverse-ISP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [trained_models/ (in repo, S7 data)](https://github.com/SenseBrainTech/overexposure-mask-reverse-ISP/tree/master/trained_models) |
| **[CIE XYZ Net: Unprocessing Images for Low-Level Computer Vision Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.12709)**<br><sub>To avoid sensor-specific RAW targets, learns to unprocess nonlinear sRGB into canonical CIE XYZ; provides a scene-referred representation for low-level restoration and color-related vision tasks. <i>Note: Paper results use the MATLAB version; the PyTorch weights are a convenience port.</i></sub> | IEEE TPAMI 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/mahmoudnafifi/CIE_XYZ_NET)<br><sub>MATLAB / PyTorch</sub> | [PyTorch/models/model_sRGB-XYZ-sRGB.pth (in repo)](https://github.com/mahmoudnafifi/CIE_XYZ_NET/tree/master/PyTorch/models) |
| **[Invertible Image Signal Processing](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/html/Xing_Invertible_Image_Signal_Processing_CVPR_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To retain RAW editability without a separate full RAW file, uses an invertible neural RAW/sRGB pipeline and differentiable JPEG simulation; trains rendering and reconstruction jointly under compression distortion.</sub> | CVPR 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/yzxing87/Invertible-ISP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained/canon.pth, nikon.pth (in repo)](https://github.com/yzxing87/Invertible-ISP/tree/main/pretrained) |
| **[CycleISP: Real Image Restoration via Improved Data Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.07761)**<br><sub>To synthesize realistic denoising pairs, learns forward and reverse camera mappings and adds sensor noise between them; generates consistent RAW/sRGB noisy-clean data rather than assuming simple noise in rendered images.</sub> | CVPR 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/swz30/CycleISP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [all models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1cHRfWPjFpTPrvBm7B4iTMEVZ4ABfjmxW?usp=sharing) |
| **[Single-Image HDR Reconstruction by Learning to Reverse the Camera Pipeline](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.01179)**<br><sub>To recover information lost by LDR rendering, uses three specialized CNNs to reverse quantization, nonlinear camera response and clipping; joint fine-tuning limits errors across the physically structured HDR reconstruction stages.</sub> | CVPR 2020 | [GitHub](https://github.com/alex04072000/SingleHDR)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> | [ckpt (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1e9vP8YPEjGcvXCa0Bfqwxw7qks7dH-VE/view?usp=sharing) |
| **[Unprocessing Images for Learned Raw Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.11127)**<br><sub>To train RAW denoisers from ordinary photographs, reverses tone, color and gain processing, injects realistic sensor noise and evaluates losses through the forward ISP; makes training account for later photographic rendering. <i>Note: Lives in a subdirectory of the google-research monorepo.</i></sub> | CVPR 2019 | [GitHub](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/unprocessing)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> | [trained models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MTFr-uaIKv5aWe7nXlhTaHBestLUiDLZ/view?usp=sharing) |

| Paper | Venue | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Edit-aware RAW Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.05859)**<br><sub>To preserve editability rather than only default-render accuracy, trains with a modular differentiable ISP whose parameters are randomly sampled; the edit-aware loss penalizes reconstruction after varied realistic photographic adjustments. <i>Note: The repo includes NILUT and tone-curve auxiliary models; the main model must be trained yourself (S24 data).</i></sub> | CVPR 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SamsungLabs/edit-aware-raw)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[MERIT: Multi-domain Efficient RAW Image Translation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20836)**<br><sub>To avoid pairwise camera-specific translators, conditions a shared multi-domain RAW generator with multiscale large-kernel attention and a sensor-noise alignment loss; contributes five-sensor paired/unpaired MDRAW data.</sub> | CVPR 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/WJ-Huang/MERIT-Multi-domain-Efficient-RAW-Image-Translation)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Improved Mapping Between Illuminations and Sensors for RAW Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14730)**<br><sub>To map RAW across sensor spectra and illuminants, studies calibrated captures from 390 illuminations, four cameras and 18 scenes; improves illumination/sensor transfer and tests synthetic data for neural-ISP training.</sub> | JOSA A 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SamsungLabs/illum-sensor-mapping) |
| **[RAW-Diffusion: RGB-Guided Diffusion Models for High-Fidelity RAW Image Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13150)**<br><sub>To synthesize sensor-specific RAW from labeled RGB collections, injects multiresolution RGB-guidance features into reverse-diffusion residual blocks; generates BDD100K-RAW/Cityscapes-RAW for data-efficient RAW object detection. <i>Note: The README does not provide weights.</i></sub> | WACV 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SonyResearch/RAW-Diffusion)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[ReRAW: RGB-to-RAW Image Reconstruction via Stratified Sampling for Efficient Object Detection on the Edge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.03782)**<br><sub>To synthesize training RAW for edge detectors, predicts gamma-space RAW candidates with a multi-head network and selects training samples by intensity strata; improves bright-pixel recovery before detector pretraining.</sub> | CVPR 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SonyResearch/ReRAW)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Generalizing ISP Model by Unsupervised Raw-to-raw Mapping](https://doi.org/10.1145/3664647.3681666)**<br><sub>To transfer an ISP without paired camera captures, predicts patchwise color-space transformation parameters with CSTPP and trains in a CycleGAN-style framework; maps sensor domains while handling spatially varying lighting.</sub> | ACM MM 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/ydxxxx/Unsupervised-Raw-to-raw-Mapping)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Rawformer: Unpaired Raw-to-Raw Translation for Learnable Camera ISPs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10700)**<br><sub>To transfer an existing neural ISP to another sensor without paired captures, learns unpaired RAW-to-RAW translation using a Transformer encoder–decoder; maps new-camera measurements into the trained ISP's sensor domain. <i>Note: The README TODO item "upload pretrained models" has not been completed.</i></sub> | ECCV 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/gosha20777/rawformer)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Graphics2RAW: Mapping Computer Graphics Images to Sensor RAW Images](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2023/html/Seo_Graphics2RAW_Mapping_Computer_Graphics_Images_to_Sensor_RAW_Images_ICCV_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To turn graphics into sensor-matched training data, uses a few RAW-DNG examples to map each rendered scene to multiple cameras and illuminants; releases 292 realistic CG images for low-light training.</sub> | ICCV 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SamsungLabs/graphics2raw) |
| **[Learning sRGB-to-Raw-RGB De-rendering with Content-Aware Metadata](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022/html/Nam_Learning_sRGB-to-Raw-RGB_De-Rendering_With_Content-Aware_Metadata_CVPR_2022_paper.html)**<br><sub>To spend reconstruction metadata where it matters, learns content-dependent sampling of original RAW values alongside a reconstruction network; online fine-tuning further adapts sRGB-to-RAW recovery to the stored samples. <i>Note: The dataset link in the README is empty.</i></sub> | CVPR 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SamsungLabs/content-aware-metadata) |
| **[Semi-Supervised Raw-to-Raw Mapping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.13883)**<br><sub>To transfer sensor color spaces with few paired captures, jointly trains on a small paired subset and larger per-camera unpaired sets; contributes two-phone RAW data for semi-supervised mapping evaluation. <i>Note: Provides DNG data and precomputed mappings.</i></sub> | BMVC 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/mahmoudnafifi/raw2raw)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Beyond Calibration: Physically Informed Learning for Raw-to-Raw Mapping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08650)**<br><sub>To maintain color across cameras and lighting, a lightweight Neural Physical Model simulates RAW under specified illumination to estimate device transformations; supports physical initialization and paired or unpaired learning.</sub> | arXiv 2025 | — |
| **[A Learnable Color Correction Matrix for RAW Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02497)**<br><sub>To synthesize RAW cheaply for driving perception, approximates inverse ISP with a learnable color-correction matrix implemented as one convolutional layer; evaluates simulated RAW for pretraining object detectors.</sub> | BMVC 2024 | — |
| **[Leveraging Frame Affinity for sRGB-to-RAW Video De-rendering](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024/html/Zhang_Leveraging_Frame_Affinity_for_sRGB-to-RAW_Video_De-rendering_CVPR_2024_paper.html)**<br><sub>To recover RAW consistently from video, extracts a temporal-affinity prior using motion and learns scene-/position-specific spatial mappings from prior frames; contributes a RAW-video de-rendering benchmark.</sub> | CVPR 2024 | — |
| **[Prior Metadata-Driven RAW Reconstruction: Eliminating the Need for Per-Image Metadata](https://doi.org/10.1145/3664647.3680819)**<br><sub>To avoid per-image metadata, searches compact offline RAW references for similar pixels and feeds retrieved priors to a neural reconstructor; compresses the reference pool to reduce search/storage cost.</sub> | ACM MM 2024 | — |
| **[SEL-CIE: Knowledge-Guided Self-Supervised Learning Framework for CIE-XYZ Reconstruction from Non-Linear sRGB Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12265)**<br><sub>To reduce paired-data requirements for linear color reconstruction, combines knowledge-guided self-supervision with available paired sRGB/XYZ images; jointly reconstructs CIE XYZ and re-renders sRGB on the sRGB2XYZ benchmark.</sub> | WSCG 2024 | — |
| **[Metadata-Based RAW Reconstruction via Implicit Neural Functions](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023/html/Li_Metadata-Based_RAW_Reconstruction_via_Implicit_Neural_Functions_CVPR_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To reconstruct RAW from sparse embedded samples without camera pretraining, fits an implicit neural function mapping coordinates and corresponding sRGB values to RAW; learns each image self-supervised from its metadata.</sub> | CVPR 2023 | — |
| **[Self-Supervised Reversed Image Signal Processing via Reference-Guided Dynamic Parameter Selection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13916)**<br><sub>To invert ISP without metadata or paired data, dynamically selects reversed-pipeline parameters from a reference RAW; generates RAW-like images matching the reference sensor/environment and tests their use in detection training.</sub> | arXiv 2023 | — |
| **[Model-Based Image Signal Processors via Learnable Dictionaries](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.03210)**<br><sub>To combine invertibility with interpretable ISP operations, learns rich parameter dictionaries inside a model-based bidirectional RAW/RGB pipeline; dictionary sampling supplies plausible augmentation even with few labeled captures. <i>Note: The mv-lab/AISP/mbispld directory contains only the paper PDF and figures.</i></sub> | AAAI 2022 | — |
| **[Reversing Image Signal Processors by Reverse Style Transferring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.09074)**<br><sub>To model ISP changes as removable style, RST-ISP-Net uses adaptive feature normalization in an end-to-end reverse-style-transfer architecture; investigates sRGB-to-RAW inversion in the AIM reversed-ISP setting.</sub> | ECCVW 2022 | — |
| **[Raw Bayer Pattern Image Synthesis for Computer Vision-oriented Image Signal Processing Pipeline Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.12823)**<br><sub>To reuse labeled color datasets for RAW perception, constrains GAN-based RGB-to-Bayer generation through an additional demosaicing transformation; supports arbitrary image sizes and evaluates end-to-end detector training on synthesized RAW.</sub> | arXiv 2021 | — |
| **[Spatially Aware Metadata for Raw Reconstruction](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/WACV2021/html/Punnappurath_Spatially_Aware_Metadata_for_Raw_Reconstruction_WACV_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To invert spatially varying tone mapping, stores spatially distributed RAW samples with the processed image and uses them for reconstruction; requires only a small sample fraction with little capture-time computation.</sub> | WACV 2021 | — |
| **[Generating Training Data for Denoising Real RGB Images via Camera Pipeline Simulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.08825)**<br><sub>To train JPEG denoisers with realistic noise, simulates RAW sensor noise and the subsequent camera pipeline; ablations identify the importance of realistic demosaicing and denoising during synthetic-data generation.</sub> | arXiv 2019 | — |
| **[Modelling the Scene Dependent Imaging in Cameras with a Deep Neural Network](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.08350)**<br><sub>To model automatic-mode processing that varies with scene content, embeds global and local context using multiscale learnable histogram layers; learns both RAW-to-sRGB and sRGB-to-RAW mappings rather than a fixed radiometric curve.</sub> | ICCV 2017 | — |

### RAW Compression & Joint Coding

Lossless/lossy RAW coding, JPEG-plus-learned-metadata reconstruction and joint rendering/compression. A rate, storage or entropy-coding objective distinguishes this category from generic inverse ISP.

**With pretrained weights (3)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Raw-JPEG Adapter: Efficient Raw Image Compression with JPEG](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19624)**<br><sub>To store linear RAW using standard JPEG, learns compact invertible spatial and optional frequency transforms and stores parameters in the JPEG comment field; reconstructs RAW with improved rate–fidelity trade-offs.</sub> | ECCV 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SamsungLabs/raw-jpeg-adapter)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [models/raw_jpeg_adapter_q_\*.pth (in repo)](https://github.com/SamsungLabs/raw-jpeg-adapter/tree/main/models) |
| **[RAWIC: Bit-Depth Adaptive Lossless Raw Image Compression](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28105)**<br><sub>To losslessly compress varying-bit-depth RAW, packs Bayer into RGGB patches and conditions a learned entropy model on each patch's bit depth; adapts probability estimates to local signal ranges. <i>Note: The README also lists a Baidu Netdisk mirror.</i></sub> | ICME 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/chunbaobao/RAWIC)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [main + ablation models (PKU Disk)](https://disk.pku.edu.cn/link/AACF89B6C4E991420B9FF93197230EA21D) |
| **[Raw Image Reconstruction with Learned Compact Metadata](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023/html/Wang_Raw_Image_Reconstruction_With_Learned_Compact_Metadata_CVPR_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To reduce RAW storage while retaining a JPEG, learns compact latent metadata and an sRGB-guided entropy context model; adaptively allocates bits to informative regions for improved reconstruction per stored bit.</sub> | CVPR 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/wyf0912/R2LCM)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Sony models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/19IFLxyreqNOWA573phNyvBUBwRwmXHtt/view?usp=sharing)<br>[Samsung models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xcEAgJztsI6QWaEpjqQzrYolKvHPzwZc/view?usp=sharing) |

| Paper | Venue | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **[MambaRaw: Selective State Space Modeling for Efficient 4K Raw Image Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24479)**<br><sub>To reconstruct 4K RAW from JPEG plus compact metadata efficiently, uses selective state-space scans on information-dense tiles and energy-aware residual refinement; models entropy with spatial/energy-coupled context. <i>Note: Must be trained separately for each λ.</i></sub> | ECCV 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Peizeli1/MambaRaw)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |

| **[RAWtoBit: A Fully End-to-end Camera ISP Network](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.07639)**<br><sub>To optimize rendering and compression together, learns a RAW-to-bitstream network under a rate–distortion objective; separate ISP and compression teachers distill task-specific knowledge into the joint model.</sub> | ECCV 2022 | — |

### ISP for Machine Vision

RAW imaging optimized or evaluated for detection, segmentation, recognition, matching, motion or robotic action. Task-reward pipeline selection stays here; general-purpose ISP search methods supporting several objectives stay under tuning.

**With pretrained weights (13)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[POS-ISP: Pipeline Optimization at the Sequence Level for Task-aware ISP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06938)**<br><sub>To avoid repeated sequential pipeline execution during search, predicts the full ISP module sequence and parameters in one pass; sequence-level reinforcement learning uses only terminal task rewards without intermediate supervision.</sub> | CVPR Findings 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/w1jyun/POS-ISP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [weights/\*.pth (in repo: LOD / LIS / KITTI)](https://github.com/w1jyun/POS-ISP/tree/main/weights) |
| **[RAWild: Sensor-Agnostic RAW Object Detection via Physics-Guided Curve and Grid Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05941)**<br><sub>To generalize detection across sensors, combines global Bézier tone correction with local bilateral-grid color adjustment driven by RAW statistics; physics-based simulation varies spectra, illumination and sensor nonidealities during training.</sub> | NeurIPS 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/I2WM/RAWild)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Checkpoints Det/Seg (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1gJlPLMO7Ty0XszLQTJkoZUIxeqbOwKqd?usp=sharing) |
| **[SimROD: A Simple Baseline for Raw Object Detection with Global and Local Enhancements](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07101)**<br><sub>To adapt detectors to RAW cheaply, learns a four-parameter global gamma transform and green-channel-guided local enhancement; combines global dynamic-range adjustment with Bayer-aware detail cues.</sub> | AAAI 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/ocean146/SimROD)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [all weights (Baidu, code 2025)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/17zEp6-Zz49M7q1O6e5cUfw)<br>[all weights (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zoT8VOwrtebnmDEtXfdQQeRvkVNoXOIx/view?usp=sharing) |
| **[Task-Aware Image Signal Processor for Advanced Visual Perception](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.13762)**<br><sub>To avoid a heavy neural renderer or rigid parameter tuning, predicts multiscale modulation operators in a compact RAW-to-RGB adapter; optimizes representations for pretrained detection/segmentation models across day and night.</sub> | CVPR 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/CVL-UESTC/TA-ISP)<br><sub>PyTorch (mmdet/mmseg)</sub> | [pretrained models (GitHub Release v0.0)](https://github.com/CVL-UESTC/TA-ISP/releases/tag/v0.0) |
| **[Dark-ISP: Enhancing RAW Image Processing for Low-Light Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.09183)**<br><sub>To align low-light rendering with detection, makes linear calibration and nonlinear tone stages differentiable and content-adaptive; physics-informed priors and a self-boost mechanism coordinate stages during task-driven training. <i>Note: README also has a Google Drive link; describes itself as the official implementation</i></sub> | ICCV 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/WildCoder566/Dark-ISP)<br><sub>PyTorch (mmdet)</sub> | [checkpoint (Baidu, code 2025)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1i9xUtQFjoFxC5mIbxJcq9A?pwd=2025) |
| **[Real-Time Scene-Adaptive Tone Mapping for High-Dynamic Range Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30400)**<br><sub>To feed HDR RAW into LDR-pretrained detectors, combines neural photometric calibration and scale-invariant local tone mapping; task-driven fine-tuning transfers detection while preserving details within real-time Jetson constraints.</sub> | NeurIPS 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/MEYE66/Real-Time-Scene-Adaptive-Tone-Mapping-for-High-Dynamic-Range-Object-Detection) | [tmo_pre.pt (in repo pretrained_model/)](https://github.com/MEYE66/Real-Time-Scene-Adaptive-Tone-Mapping-for-High-Dynamic-Range-Object-Detection/tree/HEAD/pretrained_model)<br>[Full model incl. detector (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NVflxRPlnr1naFMG_EXgVjm1M85G9Jmm?usp=sharing) |
| **[AdaptiveISP: Learning an Adaptive Image Signal Processor for Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.22939)**<br><sub>To adapt processing structure and settings per scene, trains a reinforcement-learning policy to choose ISP modules and parameters using detection rewards; jointly optimizes the pipeline rather than a fixed viewing-quality objective. <i>Note: In the README the text labels of the two ckpts are swapped relative to their file names; tell them apart by file name after downloading</i></sub> | NeurIPS 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/OpenImagingLab/AdaptiveISP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [ckpt-lod-df-1.0 (Release)](https://github.com/OpenImagingLab/AdaptiveISP/releases/download/v1.0/ckpt-lod-df-1.0.pth)<br>[ckpt-lod-df-0.98 (Release)](https://github.com/OpenImagingLab/AdaptiveISP/releases/download/v1.0/ckpt-lod-df-0.98.pth)<br>[yolov3.pt (Release)](https://github.com/OpenImagingLab/AdaptiveISP/releases/download/v1.0/yolov3.pt) |
| **[Efficient Visual Computing with Camera RAW Snapshots](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.07778)**<br><sub>To train ISP-free vision despite scarce RAW data, CycleR2R learns unpaired modular RAW/RGB mappings with a CycleGAN objective; simulated RAW adapts existing detectors and compression models to sensor measurements. <i>Note: The MultiRAW dataset is also on NJU Box.</i></sub> | IEEE TPAMI 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/njuvision/rho-vision)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [pretrained model (NJU Box)](https://box.nju.edu.cn/f/d1e199cd5ada49b88ad9/) |
| **[ISP-Teacher: Image Signal Process with Disentanglement Regularization for Unsupervised Domain Adaptive Dark Object Detection](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v38i7.28569)**<br><sub>To adapt daytime detection to unlabeled dark scenes, uses ISP-guided teacher–student learning with disentanglement regularization; couples imaging transformations and domain adaptation rather than requiring target detection labels. <i>Note: Published in the AAAI 2024 proceedings (no arXiv version); README also has a Google Drive mirror</i></sub> | AAAI 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/zhangyin1996/ISP-Teacher)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [BDD100k pretrained models (Baidu, code 1234)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1vYYKX9BdlQIHY-Y7E9n5nA?pwd=1234) |
| **[Instance Segmentation in the Dark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.14298)**<br><sub>To suppress noise in low-light segmentation features, uses adaptive weighted downsampling, smooth-oriented convolution and disturbance-suppression learning; contributes synthetic RAW augmentation and over 2,000 annotated paired captures. <i>Note: The README table links models for multiple backbones</i></sub> | IJCV 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Linwei-Chen/LIS)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [Mask R-CNN and other models (Baidu)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/16GdAxJ7GX3I9v8Mtm2xpIQ) |
| **[Image-Adaptive YOLO for Object Detection in Adverse Weather Conditions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.08088)**<br><sub>To adapt detection to fog and darkness, a small CNN predicts differentiable image-filter parameters and trains jointly with YOLOv3; learns per-image enhancement from detection feedback instead of clean-image targets.</sub> | AAAI 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/wenyyu/Image-Adaptive-YOLO)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> | [Test set and models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1P0leuiGHH69kVxyNVFuiCdCYXyYquPqM)<br>[Mirror (Baidu, code iayl)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1GQE_80rEzs0uCrzauHxwdw) |
| **[Dirty Pixels: Towards End-to-End Image Processing and Perception](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.06487)**<br><sub>To optimize imaging for recognition, jointly trains differentiable demosaicing, denoising, deblurring, tone mapping and classification; replaces isolated perceptual tuning with downstream task supervision on simulated and captured data. <i>Note: MIT License</i></sub> | ACM TOG 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/princeton-computational-imaging/DirtyPixels)<br><sub>TensorFlow</sub> | [README: code, data and trained models](https://github.com/princeton-computational-imaging/DirtyPixels) |
| **[Multitask AET with Orthogonal Tangent Regularity for Dark Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03346)**<br><sub>To separate object content from illumination degradation, jointly learns detection and auto-encoding transformations with orthogonal tangent regularization; uses synthetic low-light formation to train from ordinary labeled detection datasets. <i>Note: Baidu mirror, code 1234.</i></sub> | ICCV 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/cuiziteng/ICCV_MAET)<br><sub>PyTorch (mmdet)</sub> | [MAET-COCO (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1C7qntr0bW7piaNZPqPzpNZ0fIs8th-Qh/view?usp=sharing)<br>[MAET-EXDark (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XCP4IgW579WlGljegDCjYpQA0V3vq7-E/view?usp=sharing) |

| **[RAWDet-7: A Multi-Scenario Benchmark for Object Detection and Description on Quantized RAW Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03760)**<br><sub>To measure detection under RAW quantization, provides multicamera/multilight RAW data annotated for seven categories plus object descriptions derived from high-resolution sRGB; supports evaluation of information loss at reduced bit depth. <i>Note: Benchmark code based on MMDetection</i></sub> | TMLR 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Mishalfatima/RawDet-7) |

| **[Towards RAW Object Detection in Diverse Conditions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.15678)**<br><sub>To evaluate RAW detection in diverse weather/light, contributes 7,785 images with 62 categories and studies direct RAW pretraining; distills sRGB-model knowledge to reduce the pretraining domain gap without extra preprocessing modules. <i>Note: The README mainly covers dataset downloads (Baidu/TeraBox)</i></sub> | CVPR 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/lzyhha/AODRaw) |
| **[γ-Quant: Towards Learnable Quantization for Low-bit Pattern Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.22448)**<br><sub>To retain recognition accuracy with low sensor bandwidth, learns task-specific nonlinear quantization rather than fixed uniform levels; demonstrates RAW detection using four-bit measurements against a twelve-bit reference. <i>Note: Only the inertial-sensor part is released so far; vision experiment code is "coming later".</i></sub> | GCPR 2025 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Mishalfatima/Gamma-Quant) |
| **[RAW-Adapter: Adapting Pre-trained Visual Model to Camera RAW Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14802)**<br><sub>To reuse sRGB-pretrained detection/segmentation, learns ISP-based input adapters and intermediate model adapters for RAW; adjusts both the rendered input distribution and task-network features during adaptation. <i>Note: No weights in the README; extended version RAW-Bench at arXiv 2503.17027</i></sub> | ECCV 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/cuiziteng/ECCV_RAW_Adapter)<br><sub>PyTorch (mmdet/mmseg)</sub> |
| **[Toward RAW Object Detection: A New Benchmark and A New Model](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023/html/Xu_Toward_RAW_Object_Detection_A_New_Benchmark_and_a_New_CVPR_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To exploit HDR sensor information for detection, introduces the ROD RAW benchmark and learns image-adaptive dynamic-range adjustment jointly with a detector; analyzes effects of texture and pixel distributions. <i>Note: RAOD code is distributed with the TA-ISP repo (with a Huawei third-party notice); ROD data on Baidu, code udqg</i></sub> | CVPR 2023 | [GitHub](https://github.com/CVL-UESTC/TA-ISP/tree/main/RAOD) |
| **[GenISP: Neural ISP for Low-Light Machine Cognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03688)**<br><sub>To generalize low-light detection across sensors, first transforms RAW into device-independent color, then predicts two stages of global color parameters; trains with a frozen detector and contributes annotated RAW-NOD data. <i>Note: Third-party reimplementation; dataset at igor-morawski/RAW-NOD</i></sub> | CVPRW (NTIRE) 2022 | [GitHub (unofficial)](https://github.com/Capsar/DL-GenISP) |
| **[Crafting Object Detection in Very Low Light](https://github.com/ying-fu/LODDataset)**<br><sub>To study detection in very low light, captures paired low-/normal-light RAW images with object annotations and evaluates sensor-domain processing; provides a benchmark linking illumination restoration choices to detector performance. <i>Note: Dataset repo (Baidu, code 2021); AdaptiveISP and others provide curated versions.</i></sub> | BMVC 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/ying-fu/LODDataset) |
| **[Matching in the Dark: A Dataset for Matching Image Pairs of Low-light Scenes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.03585)**<br><sub>To benchmark local matching under extreme darkness, provides paired RAW scenes in MID and compares eight enhancement methods with eleven matching pipelines; studies whether preserved sensor precision improves feature correspondence. <i>Note: The repo provides only the MID dataset (Google Drive, about 460GB); no models.</i></sub> | ICCV 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/Wenzhengchina/Matching-in-the-Dark) |
| **[Beyond Bayer: Task-Optimal Sensor Co-Design for Robust Autonomous-Driving Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24096)**<br><sub>To optimize camera measurements for driving segmentation, differentiates a RAW-to-task pipeline through CFA and optics; controlled comparisons favor learned 2×2 CFA weights while retaining an identity PSF under the studied simulation.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[FreqAdapt: Frequency-Adaptive Processing for RAW Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03385)**<br><sub>To adapt RAW for detection efficiently, jointly encodes Fourier amplitude, phase and spatial features to predict ISP parameters; learnable frequency-aware fusion enhances task-relevant detail before the detector.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[Making the Discrete Continuous: Synthetic RAW Augmentations for Fine-Grained Evaluation of Person Detection Performance in Low Light](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22455)**<br><sub>To evaluate pedestrian detection continuously across illumination, synthesizes RAW low-light augmentations matched to the sensor-noise model; fills sparse benchmark lighting levels and compares synthetic versus real performance trends.</sub> | CVPRW 2026 | — |
| **[RawVLA: Embodied Neural Image Signal Processor For Robotic Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37530)**<br><sub>To make imaging serve robotic action, trains a streaming neural ISP for frozen vision-language-action policies after analyzing gain, noise, color, tone and bit depth; contributes RawVLA-Bench under clean/adverse capture conditions.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[UniISP: A Unified ISP Framework for Both Human and Machine Vision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07359)**<br><sub>To serve viewing and perception together, uses hybrid attention for visually supervised ISP rendering and a feature adapter that passes informative intermediate features to downstream networks; shares processing while preserving task cues.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[Beyond RGB: Adaptive Parallel Processing for RAW Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13163)**<br><sub>To replace viewing-oriented ISP for detection, learns adaptive parallel RAW-processing branches and fuses their outputs through a task-optimized Raw Adaptation Module; exposes complementary representations to the detector.</sub> | ICCV 2025 | — |
| **[Efficient Bayer-Domain Video Computer Vision with Fast Motion Estimation and Learned Perception Residual](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05990)**<br><sub>To remove redundant video perception compute, feeds Bayer directly into task models and propagates features with fast parallel motion estimation; a learned perception residual corrects motion-induced feature errors. <i>Note: Related work from the same group: Leveraging Motion Estimation for Efficient Bayer-Domain Computer Vision (arXiv 2501.15119).</i></sub> | arXiv 2025 | — |
| **[Keypoint Detection and Description for Raw Bayer Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08673)**<br><sub>To avoid full ISP for robotic local features, designs two RAW convolution kernels preserving interchannel information; jointly learns Bayer keypoints/descriptors and evaluates robustness to rotation and scale changes.</sub> | arXiv 2025 | — |
| **[Spatial-Frequency Aware for Object Detection in RAW Image](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01396)**<br><sub>To expose frequency cues to detection without opaque spectral manipulation, inverse-transforms separate frequency bands into spatial maps; fuses these with spatial features for contour- and texture-aware RAW enhancement.</sub> | arXiv 2025 | — |
| **[Adaptive Illumination Mapping for Shadow Detection in Raw Images](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2023/html/Sun_Adaptive_Illumination_Mapping_for_Shadow_Detection_in_Raw_Images_ICCV_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To retain both local and global contrast, maps high-dynamic-range RAW into multiple illumination ranges with an adaptive module; shadow-aware feedback trains the mapping alongside detection using a 7,000-image RAW benchmark.</sub> | ICCV 2023 | — |
| **[DynamicISP: Dynamically Controlled Image Signal Processor for Image Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.01146)**<br><sub>To keep task-aware processing light, controls classical ISP parameters for each frame using the previous frame's recognition result; gains adaptivity without replacing every stage with a large neural renderer.</sub> | ICCV 2023 | — |
| **[Enabling ISP-less Low-Power Computer Vision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.05451)**<br><sub>To train low-power vision without an ISP, inverts existing RGB datasets into RAW and combines direct RAW inference with analog in-pixel demosaicing; contributes RAW COCO and evaluates accuracy/energy/bandwidth trade-offs.</sub> | WACV 2023 | — |
| **[Fully Quantized Always-on Face Detector Considering Mobile Image Sensors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01001)**<br><sub>To enable always-on sensing inside image sensors, uses sensor-aware synthetic RAW with a shallow face detector and ternary weights; evaluates low-bit processing before ISP under tight compute and bandwidth constraints.</sub> | ICCVW (LBQNN) 2023 | — |
| **[Raw Instinct: Trust Your Classifiers and Skip the Conversion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.14439)**<br><sub>To test whether RGB conversion is necessary for classification, trains two CNNs on paired RAW/RGB captures and compares accuracy and total latency; contributes a dataset for direct sensor-domain recognition. <i>Note: Dataset released on Kaggle (raw-instinct).</i></sub> | PRAI 2023 | — |
| **[Raw or Cooked? Object Detection on RAW Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08965)**<br><sub>To align preprocessing with detection rather than viewing, jointly learns RAW-processing operations and detector weights; compares the learned pipeline against conventional RGB and earlier RAW methods on PASCALRAW.</sub> | SCIA 2023 | — |
| **[Rawgment: Noise-Accounted RAW Augmentation Enables Recognition in a Wide Variety of Environments](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023/html/Yoshimura_Rawgment_Noise-Accounted_RAW_Augmentation_Enables_Recognition_in_a_Wide_Variety_CVPR_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To improve recognition under unseen capture conditions, augments in RAW with explicit noise accounting and aligns noise magnitude after augmentation; reduces the sensor-noise domain gap without collecting every environment.</sub> | CVPR 2023 | — |
| **[All You Need is RAW: Defending Against Adversarial Attacks with Camera Image Pipelines](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09219)**<br><sub>To remove adversarial patterns without attack-specific training, projects RGB into learned Bayer RAW and back through a camera pipeline; uses the RAW distribution as a model-agnostic preprocessing prior.</sub> | ECCV 2022 | — |
| **[Improving the Energy Efficiency and Robustness of tinyML Computer Vision using Log-Gradient Input Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02571)**<br><sub>To reduce tinyML input bandwidth and illumination sensitivity, feeds quantized log-gradient images to CNNs; evaluates aggressive first-layer quantization, pruning potential and recognition stability across exposure changes.</sub> | arXiv 2022 | — |
| **[ISP Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.10203)**<br><sub>To skip ISP without losing pretrained recognition knowledge, distills predictions from an RGB teacher into a RAW-input student using unlabeled paired captures; adapts the input domain without new human annotations.</sub> | IEEE OJSP 2021 | — |
| **[Lightweight HDR Camera ISP for Robust Perception in Dynamic Illumination Conditions via Fourier Adversarial Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01795)**<br><sub>To maintain perception across illumination, sequentially balances light and removes noise using frequency priors; Fourier-spectrum adversarial learning regularizes a compact CNN and evaluates detection/segmentation effects.</sub> | BMVC 2021 | — |
| **[Optical Flow in the Dark](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2020/html/Zheng_Optical_Flow_in_the_Dark_CVPR_2020_paper.html)**<br><sub>To avoid enhancement breaking motion consistency, trains optical flow directly on noisy low-light images using physically synthesized RAW noise; contributes a real RAW benchmark spanning exposure levels.</sub> | CVPR 2020 | — |
| **[ISP4ML: Understanding the Role of Image Signal Processing in Efficient Deep Learning Vision Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.07954)**<br><sub>To quantify which imaging stages matter to classification, simulates a configurable sensor/ISP and trains ImageNet CNNs across pipeline settings; measures accuracy against processing cost to guide efficient vision design.</sub> | arXiv 2019 | — |
| **[Reconfiguring the Imaging Pipeline for Computer Vision](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.04352)**<br><sub>To save vision-system energy, tests eight algorithms with reversible imaging simulation and proposes configurable photography/vision modes; adjustable resolution and ADC precision enable an ISP-free low-power sensor configuration.</sub> | ICCV 2017 | — |
