### ISP Parameter & Pipeline Optimization

Optimization or prediction of conventional/differentiable ISP parameters and module sequences, with proxies, search, reinforcement learning or language guidance. Supports general-purpose and multi-objective systems. User-editable learned rendering can also appear in the controllable collection.

**With pretrained weights (1)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Goal Conditioned Reinforcement Learning for Photo Finishing Tuning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07300)**<br><sub>To tune nondifferentiable finishing pipelines efficiently, trains a goal-image-conditioned reinforcement-learning policy that treats rendering as a black box; iteratively predicts parameters for aligned targets or style references without a differentiable proxy.</sub> | NeurIPS 2024 | [GitHub](https://github.com/OpenImagingLab/RLPixTuner)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [envs/checkpoints/best_model\*.zip (in repo)](https://github.com/OpenImagingLab/RLPixTuner) |

**Code only or not released (15)**

| Paper | Venue | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **[EMOVIS: Emotion-Optimized Image Processing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03131)**<br><sub>To support expressive rather than solely fidelity-driven rendering, maps four target emotions to saturation, local tone, sharpness and other ISP controls using a calibration study; integrates these adjustments into conventional hardware stages. <i>Note: A conventional, training-free ISP control baseline rather than a neural ISP; official processing code is released, with no learned checkpoints required (checked 2026-10-28).</i></sub> | ICIP 2026 | [GitHub](https://github.com/dorbarber79/EMOVIS)<br><sub>Python / NumPy / OpenCV</sub> |
| **[DRL-ISP: Multi-Objective Camera ISP with Deep Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.03081)**<br><sub>To adapt processing to different vision objectives, a deep-RL agent repeatedly selects among 51 learned/conventional ISP tools using task-specific rewards; learns both the processing sequence and the choice of restoration/color operations. <i>Note: Includes scripts/4.copy_weights.sh and links to preprocessed data (SharePoint)</i></sub> | IROS 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/UkcheolShin/DRL-ISP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[ReconfigISP: Reconfigurable Camera Image Processing Pipeline](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.04760)**<br><sub>To adapt pipeline structure as well as parameters, trains differentiable proxies for conventional ISP modules and applies differentiable architecture search; proxy tuning maintains accuracy while optimizing sensor-, task- and efficiency-specific configurations. <i>Note: README provides the OnePlus dataset (Google Drive)</i></sub> | ICCV 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/yuke93/ReconfigISP)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[ChameleonTuner: Automatic ISP Color Tuning in Subjective Scenarios](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/WACV2026/html/Tan_ChameleonTuner_Automatic_ISP_Color_Tuning_in_Subjective_Scenarios_WACV_2026_paper.html)**<br><sub>To tune color despite viewpoint and field-of-view mismatch, establishes region-level color correspondences and searches a dedicated 3D-LUT parameter space with multiple objectives; enables interpretable subjective color tuning without pixel-aligned references. <i>Note: “We will release the code soon”</i></sub> | WACV 2026 | [GitHub (coming soon)](https://github.com/AISmartPerception/ChameleonTuner) |
| **[Language-based Color ISP Tuning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.10765)**<br><sub>To translate text descriptions into color settings, implements differentiable ISP blocks and minimizes a pretrained vision-language model's image–text objective by gradient descent; tunes conventional rendering parameters to the requested visual style.</sub> | CIC 2025 | — |
| **[Multimodal Large Language Model-Guided ISP Hyperparameter Optimization with Dynamic Preference Learning](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2025/html/Sun_Multimodal_Large_Language_Model-Guided_ISP_Hyperparameter_Optimization_with_Dynamic_Preference_ICCV_2025_paper.html)**<br><sub>To make ISP search sensitive to scene semantics and quality, incorporates MLLM-generated text descriptors and aligns preferences through DPO with dynamic pair generation; reduces manual preference labeling during hyperparameter optimization.</sub> | ICCV 2025 | — |
| **[PQDynamicISP: Dynamically Controlled Image Signal Processor for Any Image Sensors Pursuing Perceptual Quality](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10091)**<br><sub>To improve conventional ISP expressiveness without a full neural renderer, dynamically predicts global and local parameters of lightweight processing functions; one controlled pipeline adapts to image content and different sensors. <i>Note: Automatic content-dependent control, not an exposed user-editing interface; grouped with ISP parameter tuning. No official implementation was found on 2026-10-28.</i></sub> | arXiv 2024 | — |
| **[Learning to Exploit the Sequence-Specific Prior Knowledge for Image Processing Pipelines Optimization](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023/html/Qin_Learning_To_Exploit_the_Sequence-Specific_Prior_Knowledge_for_Image_Processing_CVPR_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To avoid treating ISP parameters as an unstructured vector, sequentially predicts hyperparameters using module ordering and parameter similarities; evaluates the structured predictor for detection, segmentation and image-quality objectives.</sub> | CVPR 2023 | — |
| **[Attention-Aware Learning for Hyperparameter Prediction in Image Processing Pipelines](https://www.ecva.net/papers/eccv_2022/papers_ECCV/html/4948_ECCV_2022_paper.php)**<br><sub>To replace one fixed setting for all images, learns a multi-attention mapping from RAW content to ISP parameter space with downstream-task feedback; predicts image-specific settings for detection, segmentation and human viewing.</sub> | ECCV 2022 | — |
| **[Neural Photo-Finishing](https://doi.org/10.1145/3550454.3555526)**<br><sub>To retain fine-grained controls while enabling gradients, concatenates tailored neural proxies of individual legacy finishing steps; supports image/video style transfer, ISP slider regression and photography-driven neural demosaicing.</sub> | SIGGRAPH Asia (TOG) 2022 | — |
| **[End-to-End High Dynamic Range Camera Pipeline Optimization](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/html/Robidoux_End-to-End_High_Dynamic_Range_Camera_Pipeline_Optimization_CVPR_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To optimize HDR imaging for downstream tasks, jointly tunes ISP hyperparameters and detector weights with mixed zeroth-/first-order block-coordinate descent; augments RAW with emulated SNR-transition artifacts to account for sensor behavior.</sub> | CVPR 2021 | — |
| **[Reinforcement Learning of Self Enhancing Camera Image and Signal Processing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07499)**<br><sub>To remove heterogeneous patch artifacts, clusters variational-autoencoder features and trains a soft actor–critic agent to transform noisy patches toward nearby clean subspaces; recursive self-enhancement and reward-based deblocking refine the result.</sub> | arXiv 2021 | — |
| **[Hardware-in-the-loop End-to-end Optimization of Camera Image Processing Pipelines](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2020/html/Mosleh_Hardware-in-the-Loop_End-to-End_Optimization_of_Camera_Image_Processing_Pipelines_CVPR_2020_paper.html)**<br><sub>To tune actual hardware without proxy errors, interfaces a zeroth-order stochastic multiobjective solver directly with the ISP; optimizes domain-specific losses for detection, segmentation or viewing using hardware-in-the-loop feedback.</sub> | CVPR 2020 | — |
| **[Hyperparameter Optimization in Black-box Image Processing using Differentiable Proxies](https://doi.org/10.1145/3306346.3322996)**<br><sub>To optimize black-box ISP settings for arbitrary objectives, trains a CNN mapping configuration space directly to evaluation metrics with hardware-in-the-loop; first-order search avoids explicitly approximating each lower-level image transformation.</sub> | SIGGRAPH (TOG) 2019 | — |
| **[Automatic ISP Image Quality Tuning using Non-linear Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.09023)**<br><sub>To reduce expert tuning effort across ISP blocks, combines nonlinear optimization with automatic reference generation and image-quality objectives; treats denoising, demosaicing and sharpening implementations as black boxes.</sub> | ICIP 2018 | — |

### Challenges, Surveys & Evaluation

Challenge reports, surveys, evaluation protocols and position papers. A report is counted once; separately released solutions are implementation resources nested under that publication. Dataset papers stay with the task they benchmark.

**With pretrained weights (3)**

| Paper | Venue | Code | Weights |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Learned Smartphone ISP on Mobile GPUs with Deep Learning, Mobile AI & AIM 2022 Challenge: Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.03885)**<br><sub>To optimize neural ISP for real phone GPUs, benchmarks TensorFlow Lite models on paired UltraISP data and Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 hardware; reports rendering fidelity alongside measured mobile latency.</sub> | ECCVW 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/mv-lab/AISP)<br><sub>TensorFlow Lite</sub> | [mai22-learnedisp/model.tflite + .h5 (baseline)](https://github.com/mv-lab/AISP/tree/main/mai22-learnedisp) |
| **[AIM 2020 Challenge on Learned Image Signal Processing Pipeline](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.04994)**<br><sub>To benchmark learned phone-to-DSLR rendering, maps Huawei P20 RAW to Canon references and combines fidelity metrics with user-study perception; reviews submitted demosaicing, restoration and color-mapping pipelines.<br><b>Implementation: MW-ISPNet.</b> For the AIM 2020 phone-RAW-to-DSLR benchmark, MW-ISPNet combines a U-Net, multilevel wavelets and residual channel attention for restoration and color rendering; the linked publication is the challenge report documenting this solution.</sub> | ECCVW 2020 | MW-ISPNet: [GitHub](https://github.com/cszhilu1998/MW-ISPNet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [MW-ISPNet · Track1 models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1lt5eXn49LgLzdj3z7k7lPK0B7obiLIHd?usp=sharing)<br>[MW-ISPNet · Track2 models (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1uyU1huZnh8Wf7BYFkXVfrTl64EuFNcO7?usp=sharing) |
| **[NTIRE 2020 Challenge on Real Image Denoising: Dataset, Methods and Results](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.04117)**<br><sub>To compare real-noise removal in sensor and display spaces, introduces SIDD+ evaluation data and separate Bayer/sRGB tracks; reviews submitted models under a shared denoising protocol.<br><b>Implementation: MWRCANet.</b> For real Bayer-noise removal, combines multilevel wavelet decomposition and residual channel attention to aggregate restoration features; the linked NTIRE 2020 report documents the RAW-track solution and the SIDD+ evaluation protocol.</sub> | CVPRW 2020 | MWRCANet: [GitHub](https://github.com/happycaoyue/NTIRE20_raw_image_denoising_winner_MWRCANet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> | [MWRCANet · RAW model dn_mwrcanet_raw_c1.pth (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1T23SqUEE1_oGGBK-gaRJ3L1jfVctRQtX?usp=sharing)<br>[MWRCANet · Mirror (Baidu, code 0odp)](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1Hbo86y3NYYf-WtLONRH3Sg) |

| **[MIPI 2022 Challenge on Quad-Bayer Re-mosaic: Dataset and Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.07060)**<br><sub>To reuse Bayer pipelines with Quad sensors, defines full-resolution Quad-to-Bayer interpolation jointly with denoising; contributes sensor data and a common challenge evaluation of submitted remosaicing methods.</sub> | ECCVW (MIPI) 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/mipi-challenge/MIPI2022) |
| **[MIPI 2022 Challenge on RGBW Sensor Re-mosaic: Dataset and Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.08471)**<br><sub>To convert RGBW sensor measurements into standard Bayer, benchmarks full-resolution remosaicing and denoising; supplies sensor-specific data and compares algorithms under a shared reconstruction protocol. <i>Note: The repo lists data and winning-solution links for each track.</i></sub> | ECCVW (MIPI) 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/mipi-challenge/MIPI2022) |

AIM 2022 Challenge Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11153)**<br><sub>To recover sensor-like images from ordinary RGB without metadata, defines two smartphone inverse-ISP tracks; reports baselines and submitted RAW-reconstruction methods for downstream restoration-data generation.</sub> | ECCVW 2022 | [GitHub](https://github.com/mv-lab/AISP/tree/main/aim22-reverseisp) |
| **[NTIRE 2021 Challenge on Burst Super-Resolution: Methods and Results](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021W/NTIRE/html/Bhat_NTIRE_2021_Challenge_on_Burst_Super-Resolution_Methods_and_Results_CVPRW_2021_paper.html)**<br><sub>To benchmark 4× reconstruction from noisy RAW bursts, separates synthetic and real-handheld tracks; compares alignment, fusion and reconstruction designs for joint denoising, demosaicing and super-resolution. <i>Note: Official toolkit and test sets.</i></sub> | CVPRW 2021 | [GitHub](https://github.com/goutamgmb/NTIRE21_BURSTSR) |
| **[A Reference-Free Framework for Evaluating Single-Frame ISP Pipelines](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23321)**<br><sub>To estimate pipeline quality without a clean image, predicts a proxy sRGB reference from output/ISO and computes standard full-reference metrics against it; lightweight LoRA adapts the evaluator when ISP components change.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[NTIRE 2026 Challenge on Learned Smartphone ISP with Unpaired Data: Methods and Results](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2026W/NTIRE/html/Perevozchikov_NTIRE_2026_Challenge_on_Learned_Smartphone_ISP_with_Unpaired_Data_CVPRW_2026_paper.html)**<br><sub>To benchmark ISP learning without matched captures, introduces UP-ISP with over 900 Pixel 6 scenes and a common RAW-to-sRGB protocol; reports the official baseline and competing unpaired training strategies.</sub> | CVPRW 2026 | — |
| **[The Need for Neural ISP in the Small-Pixel Era: How Shrinking Pixels Push Optics to the Limit and Neural Restoration Pushes Back](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07675)**<br><sub>To test whether neural restoration compensates shrinking pixels, simulates a telephoto module at five pixel pitches and compares stagewise versus learned ISP; analyzes residual optical aberrations and low-SNR multiframe recovery.</sub> | arXiv 2026 | — |
| **[A Comprehensive Survey on Image Signal Processing Approaches for Low-Illumination Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05995)**<br><sub>To organize low-illumination enhancement methods, reviews traditional, deep-learning and hybrid processing approaches; compares how they handle brightness, contrast, noise and detail within an ISP-oriented taxonomy.</sub> | arXiv 2025 | — |
| **[AIM 2025 Challenge on Real-World RAW Image Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06601)**<br><sub>To test synthetic-data-driven denoising across cameras, benchmarks real low-light RAW from five DSLRs; compares noise synthesis, architectures and training using both full-reference fidelity and no-reference quality metrics.</sub> | ICCVW 2025 | — |
| **[AIM 2025 Low-light RAW Video Denoising Challenge: Dataset, Methods and Results](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.16830)**<br><sub>To evaluate sensor-specific temporal denoising, provides 756 ten-frame sequences from 14 phone sensors with burst-averaged references; ranks Bayer-preserving final-frame outputs using PSNR/SSIM across light/exposure conditions.</sub> | ICCVW 2025 | — |
| **[Learned Smartphone ISP on Mobile GPUs, Mobile AI 2025 Challenge: Report](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025W/MAI/html/Ignatov_Learned_Smartphone_ISP_on_Mobile_GPUs_Mobile_AI_2025_Challenge_CVPRW_2025_paper.html)**<br><sub>To assess deployable learned smartphone ISP, reviews mobile-GPU RAW-to-RGB challenge methods and their quality/runtime trade-offs; documents the benchmark and competing pipeline designs rather than introducing one standalone model.</sub> | CVPRW 2025 | — |
| **[NTIRE 2025 Challenge on Night Photography Rendering](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025W/NTIRE/html/Ershov_NTIRE_2025_Challenge_on_Night_Photography_Rendering_CVPRW_2025_paper.html)**<br><sub>To compare night rendering against a professional-camera reference, captures smartphone/camera pairs through a beam splitter; evaluates objective PSNR/SSIM and viewer similarity scores, documenting the competing neural/conventional pipelines.</sub> | CVPRW 2025 | — |
| **[NTIRE 2025 Challenge on RAW Image Restoration and Super-Resolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02197)**<br><sub>To benchmark blind sensor-domain restoration, defines RAW denoising/deblurring and 2× Bayer SR tasks under unknown degradations; reviews submitted methods and results for integration into camera pipelines.</sub> | CVPRW 2025 | — |
| **[RAW Image Reconstruction from RGB on Smartphones. NTIRE 2025 Challenge Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01947)**<br><sub>To generate smartphone RAW without capture metadata, benchmarks inverse ISP from matching sRGB images; documents the reconstruction dataset, baseline and submitted efficient models for reusable RAW-data synthesis.</sub> | CVPRW 2025 | — |
| **[Deep RAW Image Super-Resolution. A NTIRE 2024 Challenge Survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16223)**<br><sub>To compare blind RAW super-resolution, tasks models with 2× Bayer upscaling under unknown blur/noise; reviews the top submissions using a shared evaluation setup for sensor-domain reconstruction.</sub> | CVPRW 2024 | — |
| **[MIPI 2024 Challenge on Demosaic for HybridEVS Camera: Methods and Results](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04867)**<br><sub>To evaluate HybridEVS reconstruction with interleaved event pixels, benchmarks RAW-to-color demosaicing solutions and compares their reconstruction strategies; documents a sensor-specific challenge rather than a general image-restoration backbone.</sub> | CVPRW 2024 | — |
| **[MIPI 2024 Challenge on Few-shot RAW Image Denoising: Methods and Results](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07006)**<br><sub>To reduce camera-calibration data requirements, benchmarks few-shot RAW denoising under a shared challenge protocol; reviews submitted noise modeling, adaptation and reconstruction solutions and their measured results.</sub> | CVPRW 2024 | — |
| **[NTIRE 2024 Challenge on Night Photography Rendering](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024W/NTIRE/html/Ershov_NTIRE_2024_Challenge_on_Night_Photography_Rendering_CVPRW_2024_paper.html)**<br><sub>To balance night-photo quality and mobile efficiency, evaluates smartphone RAW rendering by viewer preference and execution time; reports separate quality/efficiency nominations and the top processing pipelines.</sub> | CVPRW 2024 | — |
| **[ISP meets Deep Learning: A Survey on Deep Learning Methods for Image Signal Processing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11994)**<br><sub>To connect learned ISP stages with full pipelines, surveys deep methods for demosaicing, denoising and enhancement alongside end-to-end RAW rendering; compares datasets/results and identifies limitations for future research.</sub> | ACM Computing Surveys 2023 | — |
| **[MIPI 2023 Challenge on RGBW Remosaic: Methods and Results](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.10551)**<br><sub>To process RGBW sensors with existing Bayer pipelines, benchmarks joint remosaicing/denoising and compares top methods using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS and distribution metrics; documents the challenge protocol and results.</sub> | CVPRW (MIPI) 2023 | — |
| **[NTIRE 2023 Challenge on Night Photography Rendering](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023W/NTIRE/html/Shutova_NTIRE_2023_Challenge_on_Night_Photography_Rendering_CVPRW_2023_paper.html)**<br><sub>To test night rendering with limited target-sensor data, supplies calibrated color-checker captures instead of a large training set; compares RAW-to-sRGB solutions through viewer and photographer preference rankings.</sub> | CVPRW 2023 | — |
| **[NTIRE 2022 Burst Super-Resolution Challenge](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022W/NTIRE/html/Bhat_NTIRE_2022_Burst_Super-Resolution_Challenge_CVPRW_2022_paper.html)**<br><sub>To compare multiframe reconstruction, requires 4× RGB output from noisy RAW bursts, jointly testing denoising/demosaicing/SR; separates pixel-aligned synthetic data from real handheld bursts with approximate DSLR references.</sub> | CVPRW 2022 | — |
| **[NTIRE 2022 Challenge on Night Photography Rendering](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022W/NTIRE/html/Ershov_NTIRE_2022_Challenge_on_Night_Photography_Rendering_CVPRW_2022_paper.html)**<br><sub>To assess subjective night rendering, evaluates RAW-to-sRGB outputs using mean viewer opinions followed by professional-photographer ranking; documents thirteen teams' pipelines and their visual-quality results.</sub> | CVPRW 2022 | — |
| **[Learned Smartphone ISP on Mobile NPUs with Deep Learning, Mobile AI 2021 Challenge: Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.07809)**<br><sub>To measure learned ISP on mobile NPUs, provides Sony Quad-Bayer RAW/medium-format RGB pairs and evaluates NPU-compatible models; reports both reconstruction fidelity and actual full-HD processing latency.</sub> | CVPRW 2021 | — |
| **[AIM 2019 Challenge on RAW to RGB Mapping: Methods and Results](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICCVW.2019.00443)**<br><sub>To establish real smartphone-to-DSLR ISP evaluation, benchmarks RAW-to-RGB reconstruction combining demosaicing, denoising and color rendering; documents participating solutions and fidelity/perceptual results on cross-camera data.</sub> | ICCVW 2019 | — |

## Tools & Open-source ISPs

**RAW I/O**

- [rawpy](https://github.com/letmaik/rawpy) - Reads nearly all camera RAW / DNG files and performs basic post-processing; the de facto standard for preprocessing RAW datasets. <sub>Python</sub>
- [LibRaw](https://github.com/LibRaw/LibRaw) - Successor of dcraw; extracts RAW pixels, CFA pattern, black level, white balance and other metadata from almost every camera format. <sub>C++</sub>

**Classical ISP Pipelines & Algorithms**

- [fast-openISP](https://github.com/QiuJueqin/fast-openISP) - Complete traditional ISP pipeline (BLC, DPC, demosaicing, AWB, CCM, gamma, denoising, sharpening); a convenient classical reference next to learned models. <sub>Python / NumPy</sub>
- [openISP](https://github.com/cruxopen/openISP) - An early open-source reference implementation of a traditional ISP. <sub>Python</sub>
- [Infinite-ISP](https://github.com/10x-Engineers/Infinite-ISP) - Traditional ISP algorithms organized by hardware ISP module, with learned modules planned. <sub>Python</sub>
- [simple-camera-pipeline](https://github.com/AbdoKamel/simple-camera-pipeline) - Lightweight RAW→sRGB camera pipeline (MATLAB / Python), commonly used to render SIDD and similar data. <sub>MATLAB / Python</sub>
- [ISP-pipeline-hdrplus](https://github.com/jhfmat/ISP-pipeline-hdrplus) - Traditional ISP implementation with HDR+ multi-frame fusion and calibration tools; test images and tools are on Baidu (code aaaa). <sub>Python</sub>
- [colour-demosaicing](https://github.com/colour-science/colour-demosaicing) - Classical CFA demosaicing algorithms (bilinear, Malvar 2004, Menon 2007 DDFAPD) for Bayer mosaics. <sub>Python</sub>
- [colour](https://github.com/colour-science/colour) - Color science toolbox: color spaces, chromatic adaptation, color-checker data and color-difference metrics such as CIEDE2000. <sub>Python</sub>
- [hdr-plus](https://github.com/timothybrooks/hdr-plus) - Open implementation of the HDR+ burst align-and-merge pipeline. <sub>C++ / Halide</sub>

**Learned-ISP Toolboxes**

- [mv-lab/AISP](https://github.com/mv-lab/AISP) - Learned-ISP toolbox by Marcos Conde et al.: RAW degradation generation, challenge baselines, LPIENet, NILUT and more. <sub>PyTorch / TF</sub>

**RAW Developers**

- [darktable](https://github.com/darktable-org/darktable) - Open-source RAW developer with a modular, scene-referred processing pipeline. <sub>C</sub>
- [RawTherapee](https://github.com/Beep6581/RawTherapee) - Open-source RAW developer with many demosaicing, denoising and tone-mapping options. <sub>C++</sub>

## Learning Resources

**Tutorials and surveys**

- [Understanding the In-Camera Rendering Pipeline and the Role of AI/Deep Learning](http://www.eecs.yorku.ca/~mbrown/ICCV2023_Brown.html) - Michael S. Brown (ICCV 2023 tutorial). Color science, the conventional ISP stages, and where deep learning is changing them; slides are online.
- [Mobile Computational Photography: A Tour](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-vision-093019-115521) - Delbracio, Kelly, Brown, Milanfar (Annual Review of Vision Science 2021). Survey of the phone camera pipeline, from burst merging to learned processing.
- [Processing RAW Images in MATLAB](https://rcsumner.net/raw_guide/RAWguide.pdf) - Rob Sumner. Step-by-step guide from a RAW file to a displayable image, with code.
- [Color Image Processing Pipeline](https://doi.org/10.1109/MSP.2005.1407713) - Ramanath, Snyder, Yoo, Drew (IEEE Signal Processing Magazine 2005). Classic overview of the stages of a digital still camera pipeline.
- [A Software Platform for Manipulating the Camera Imaging Pipeline](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-46448-0_26) - Karaimer and Brown (ECCV 2016). Exposes every stage of a camera pipeline so intermediate results can be inspected and modified.

**Books**

- [Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications, 2nd ed.](https://szeliski.org/Book/) - Richard Szeliski (2022). Free online; chapter 2.3 covers the digital camera and image formation.
- [Image Sensors and Signal Processing for Digital Still Cameras](https://doi.org/10.1201/9781420026856) - Junichi Nakamura (ed.), CRC Press. Sensor physics, noise and the processing chain of digital still cameras.

**Classical papers behind each stage**

- Noise
  - [Radiometric CCD Camera Calibration and Noise Estimation](https://doi.org/10.1109/34.276126) - Healey and Kondepudy, TPAMI 1994
  - [Practical Poissonian-Gaussian Noise Modeling and Fitting for Single-Image Raw-Data](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIP.2008.2001399) - Foi et al., TIP 2008
  - [Image Denoising by Sparse 3-D Transform-Domain Collaborative Filtering (BM3D)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIP.2007.901238) - Dabov et al., TIP 2007
  - [Optimal Inversion of the Generalized Anscombe Transformation for Poisson-Gaussian Noise](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIP.2012.2202675) - Mäkitalo and Foi, TIP 2013
- Demosaicing
  - [High-Quality Linear Interpolation for Demosaicing of Bayer-Patterned Color Images](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICASSP.2004.1326587) - Malvar, He and Cutler, ICASSP 2004
  - [Adaptive Homogeneity-Directed Demosaicing Algorithm](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIP.2004.838691) - Hirakawa and Parks, TIP 2005
  - [Demosaicking: Color Filter Array Interpolation](https://doi.org/10.1109/MSP.2005.1407714) - Gunturk et al., IEEE Signal Processing Magazine 2005
- White balance
  - [A Spatial Processor Model for Object Colour Perception (gray world)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0016-0032(80)90058-7) - Buchsbaum, Journal of the Franklin Institute 1980
  - [Edge-Based Color Constancy (gray edge)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIP.2007.901808) - van de Weijer, Gevers and Gijsenij, TIP 2007
  - [Computational Color Constancy: Survey and Experiments](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIP.2011.2118224) - Gijsenij, Gevers and van de Weijer, TIP 2011
- Tone mapping and HDR
  - [Recovering High Dynamic Range Radiance Maps from Photographs](https://doi.org/10.1145/258734.258884) - Debevec and Malik, SIGGRAPH 1997
  - [Photographic Tone Reproduction for Digital Images](https://doi.org/10.1145/566654.566575) - Reinhard et al., SIGGRAPH 2002
  - [Exposure Fusion](https://doi.org/10.1109/PG.2007.17) - Mertens, Kautz and Van Reeth, Pacific Graphics 2007
- Burst photography
  - [Burst Photography for High Dynamic Range and Low-Light Imaging on Mobile Cameras (HDR+)](https://doi.org/10.1145/2980179.2980254) - Hasinoff et al., SIGGRAPH Asia 2016
  - [Handheld Multi-Frame Super-Resolution](https://doi.org/10.1145/3306346.3323024) - Wronski et al., SIGGRAPH 2019

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome: a missing paper, a newly released checkpoint, or a dead link. All content lives in the YAML files under [`data/`](data/), with Chinese overlays under `data/i18n/`; both languages of the README, weights index and interactive page are generated from them. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the entry format and the inclusion rules.

## About This List

**How entries were collected.** Candidates came from keyword screening of all CVPR, ICCV and WACV papers on CVF Open Access (2017-2026), the CVF workshops (NTIRE, Mobile AI, MIPI, AIM and others), ECCV 2018-2024 on ECVA, NeurIPS 2019-2024, reverse-chronological arXiv title searches (raw, bayer, ISP, demosaicing, color constancy, low-light raw, burst, neural/learned ISP, RGB-to-RAW), and the lists under [Related Lists](#related-lists). GitHub repository search was used to find code for papers that do not link any.

**How code and weights were checked.** Each repository README (and, where needed, its file tree) was read on 2026-10-11. The weight links are the ones the README gives, including extraction codes for Baidu Netdisk. No checkpoint was downloaded or run, and hosted files can disappear; please open an issue or PR when a link breaks or new weights appear. Checkpoints remain under their authors' licenses.

**Known gaps.** This curated index is not an exhaustive survey; newly released proceedings may be missing. AAAI, ACM MM, TIP, TPAMI, IJCV and BMVC are covered through arXiv, so journal-only papers may be missing. Deliberately out of scope: general restoration backbones (SwinIR, Restormer, NAFNet), enhancement or denoising that only operates on sRGB, RAW-domain NeRF / 3DGS reconstruction, and multispectral or polarization demosaicing.
